# Part I: US agent-memory market audit

## US agent-memory market: 3×3 adversarial audit versus ai-memory v1.0.0

**Assessment date:** 2026-09-27 UTC · **Task:** U5-SYNTH-DOC · **Analyst:** Codex, gpt-6-astra, high reasoning · **Tracking:** #4055 · **Status:** evidence-weighted market synthesis, not a security certification.

### 1. Provenance and decision authority

This document synthesizes an exhaustive-search effort across the US market: three web sweeps (open source; hyperscalers and enterprise vendors; startups and federal/defense suppliers), followed by a **3×3 adversarial audit**: three independent assessment lenses, three adversarial challenges and three final voters (enterprise CIO, federal CISO and AI-platform architect). “Exhaustive” describes the intended breadth and reconciliation of the recorded searches, not proof that every offering in existence was found. The resulting registry contains **127 distinct offering rows**, with aliases grouped explicitly, including every candidate in the supplied sweeps/consolidation, the nine original #4055 competitors, and ai-memory. **58 candidates received this US audit's final ballots.**

The binding decision source is `us3x3/TALLY.json`, SHA-256 `c2002a98bd313e81bd5587ce1ad28d56518741eb8ecf76b141493b3419cbef1a`. Every decision and every vote count in that tally appears in §4, including minority votes. No assessment-lens score, discovery label, funding fact or new source refresh silently changes a ballot. A NO-CONSENSUS decision remains NO-CONSENSUS; the current US tally contains none, while earlier #4055 results retain two such outcomes in §5. The IDs in the final `U0-CONSOLIDATE-CANDIDATES.json` control joins; several U1 filenames and `U0-candidates.json` use stale numbering.

**ai-memory authority:** only CodeGraph queries with `--path /home/fate_two/v07/v09-dev` and `git -C /mnt/t9/v07/v09-dev show origin/release/v1.0.0:<path>` were used for implementation verification. The operator specifies code equivalence to `a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940`; immutable citations use that SHA. CodeGraph is navigation, and release blobs control any discrepancy with emitted on-disk snippets. The source declares AlphaOne LLC, version 1.0.0 and Apache-2.0. US ownership by a US citizen is **OPERATOR-ATTESTED**, not inferred from source. No checkout was modified. [Cargo.toml:1](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/Cargo.toml#L1)

**Evidence levels:** CODE means static implementation inspection at the pinned SHA, not an executed system test. DOC-LEVEL means official product, corporate or government documentation **unverified in implementation code**. SCREEN-ONLY means discovery material was not sufficient for implementation assurance. An open SDK does not make its managed backend open; an authorization listing documents a service boundary, not every feature, region or customer installation. All ownership/funding/HQ statements are documentary or operator-attested, even on CODE rows.

### 2. Executive answer

**Yes: at least one US-owned offering is above ai-memory for the combined enterprise/federal agent-memory procurement lens — YES 3/3.** Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory is **ABOVE 3/3 overall, STRONGER 3/3 federally**. H2O.ai and C3 AI are each **ABOVE 2/3 overall, ON_PAR 1/3; STRONGER 3/3 federally**. H2O's US office evidence does not prove ultimate domestic control; AWS's documented US corporate parent independently establishes the existential result. These are procurement-weighted outcomes, not matched recall/latency results or dominance on every feature.

AWS has a concrete memory service in GovCloud US-West and AgentCore is listed inside the High/Class D boundary. IAM/resource policies, default service encryption, optional customer KMS and supported operations are substantive advantages over ai-memory's current assurance evidence. It cannot replace a fully disconnected, independently operated endpoint. **No universal winner above ai-memory for every air-gapped endpoint configuration is established.** [DOC-LEVEL: Memory GovCloud availability](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/agentcore-memory-policy-harness-govcloud/), [AgentCore authorization scope](https://aws.amazon.com/compliance/services-in-scope/FedRAMP/).

H2O documents editable/shareable persistent memory blocks, enterprise identity and private deployment; C3 documents long-term agent memory and customer-hosted delivery. Their enterprise/federal strengths outweigh ai-memory's unresolved readiness under two voters' overall weighting. Exact new memory release/model inclusion in authorized packages remains a procurement question. H2O's government cloud authorization does not certify a customer's air gap. C3's historical USAF CBM+/PANDA IL5 ATO is not blanket authorization of current Generative AI Memory. [DOC-LEVEL: H2O memory](https://docs.h2o.ai/enterprise-h2ogpte/v1.7.3/guide/memory/create-and-manage-memory-blocks), [H2O federal record](https://www.fedramp.gov/marketplace/products/FR2521554684/), [C3 memory](https://docs.c3.ai/docs/genAiSearch/8.10/topic/genai-dev-agent-memories-feature), [SMX/Elevate IAP record](https://www.fedramp.gov/marketplace/products/F1603077867/).

**Where ai-memory leads in evidenced scope:** a directly inspectable Apache-licensed Rust endpoint substrate combining SQLite operation, native MCP/CLI/HTTP surfaces, optional Postgres+AGE+pgvector, independently operated memory-peer replication, record provenance/signatures, deterministic authority checks and a durable inbox with local rust-a2a wake hints. These are useful integrated mechanisms, particularly where local custody and operator autonomy are requirements. They do not establish best retrieval, universal default-deny security, complete signed logging, fleet convergence, or independent fail-closed LLM judges at this pin.[^AI-S][^AI-M]

**Where others lead:** achieved federal service authorizations and enterprise identity/key administration; managed operational support and documented deployment scale; model-role configurability; graph/temporal learned memory and application orchestration. Vestige and ContextLattice also implement cryptographic receipts/anchors, so ai-memory has no audit exclusivity. Microsoft Agent Framework, Mastra and CrewAI provide stronger standard-A2A/application composition. Zep and Google Memory Bank expose stronger managed IAM/KMS contracts. Funding or adoption alone is not a security or quality score. Specific final votes remain in §4; these narrower comparisons do not manufacture additional ballots.

### 3. Search method, coverage and exclusions

Sweep A queried GitHub topics/descriptions including agent-memory, llm-memory, mcp-memory, long-term-memory, memgpt and ai-memory, used a >300-star discovery filter (about 130 repositories), and examined 253 memory-related links from an MCP directory plus web roundups/vendor leads. Sweep B searched official cloud/vendor memory APIs, deployment/security documentation and service authorization scope. Sweep C searched startup/YC records, federal vendors, FedRAMP records and SBIR/AFWERX/DIU context; its SBIR API request returned 403, so an absent award is not proof that none exists. The three sweeps' positive and negative claims were hypotheses: U1 dossiers, U2 assessments, U3 attacks and U4 votes corrected them. In particular, the older federal feed, static product-name matching, broad “no memory substrate” assertions and ai-memory's supplied judge/default assumptions were not final evidence.

US qualification in the original consolidation was **US-owned OR US-headquartered**. That is broader than demonstrated US ownership. The registry distinguishes a US corporate operator/parent from a mere US office/profile. **US-OWNED here is the ordinary corporate-domicile/parent sense, with beneficial ownership and citizenship UNVERIFIED unless explicitly attested.** It does not certify a US-person-only cap table, workforce, supply chain or operational access. UNVERIFIED is intentionally a third value where a binary national label would be guesswork.

Foreign/eligibility-held offerings remain visible: Caura (Israeli legal entity), Cohere North (Canada), Weaviate (Netherlands), Memgraph (UK), cognee (Germany), PRC-associated OpenViking/ByteDance and Tencent, and individually maintained projects with foreign profile locations. KIP, ruflo, MemPalace and several other projects lack sufficient ownership/HQ evidence; they are not assigned a country from names or language. **deepset correction:** its German imprint coexists with a Delaware Deepset, Inc. contracting entity. Ultimate parent/control is UNVERIFIED, so a categorical “wholly foreign-owned” conclusion is unwarranted. This correction does not create a new ballot or erase Haystack's historical NO-CONSENSUS. Elastic's Netherlands parent and Trace's unresolved legal location cannot establish the US-owned YES. [deepset imprint](https://www.deepset.ai/imprint), [contracting entities](https://www.deepset.ai/terms-and-conditions).

Registry completeness is reconciliation against these supplied artifacts, not a census of every repository behind the directory searches. Aliases share a row when they are one assessed offering/family; unrelated namesakes remain separate: Mem0 OpenMemory versus CaviraOSS LongMemory, Activeloop Hivemind versus Shield AI Hivemind, and Engram.com versus Weaviate Engram. SDKs for AWS/Google and Microsoft framework lineage are named in their rows. Federal delivery channels and the unverified LeapfrogAI successor are retained as adjacent screen-only rows. No new competitors were cloned in synthesis; existing US-path source clones and pinned raw-source reads were used. Temporary material stayed under `/mnt/t9/tmp/deputy`, never `/tmp`.

#### 3c. Secure swarm / cluster / hive memory matrix

Y = supported within the stated scope; PARTIAL = optional, incomplete, dependent on another component, or subject to a material defect; N = bounded negative established for the assessed implementation/contract; UNVERIFIED = evidence is insufficient. BASIC means shared context/scopes; ADVANCED means additional identity/coordination/orchestration machinery, **not a certification of safe isolation**. NONE/VIA-FRAMEWORK/NATIVE characterize communications; native internal messaging is separately distinguished from the standard Agent2Agent protocol. “Securely” requires a deployment-level result across identity, isolation, transport, storage, evidence and operation. A cryptographic commitment proves integrity of captured data, not its truth, completeness or authorization.

The row footnotes supply pinned file:line evidence for CODE and official URLs for DOC. Screen-only N/“not found” entries from the original sweeps are translated to UNVERIFIED, because discovery absence is not implementation absence. No screened row receives an enterprise pass. Endpoint credit does not automatically mean every inference role, control plane and update path has passed a network-denial test. A Y audit-log cell can coexist with UNVERIFIED signed attestation; these are different requirements.

**All-column conclusion: none is established to meet every column.** This is an evidence finding, not proof that no vendor can build such a deployment. Exact near-miss gaps under the table's conjunctive criterion:

- **ai-memory:** secure isolation/coordination remains PARTIAL because enrollment/default posture and open defects matter; at-rest protection is optional/content-only with no established native KMS; cryptographic audit and ordinary logging are incomplete on known paths; enterprise failure closure is not universal. Native AWH1 wake does not satisfy a separate requirement for standard A2A. Full air-gap acceptance and backend/interface parity are unverified. TLS listener refusal itself earns Y.
- **AWS AgentCore Memory:** no independent endpoint/air-gap distribution; Runtime A2A is VIA-FRAMEWORK for Memory; CloudTrail signed digests are optional/platform-level rather than per-memory attestations. Identity must be bound by the application. Its achieved federal advantage remains real despite these missing columns.
- **Vestige:** limited multi-agent isolation/coordination, no native inbox/task plane, plaintext native HTTP, optional local-store encryption/signing, and incomplete governance/audit coverage prevent a full pass. Its encrypted archives and atomic receipts are genuine strengths.
- **ContextLattice and MemPalace:** transport/default identity and complete encrypted storage/forensic audit remain insufficient; ContextLattice also has the omitted-key admission flaw and no verified live native A2A plane. MemPalace has real native logstream coordination/anti-entropy, but not established fine-grained authenticated enterprise tenancy.
- **Zep and Google Memory Bank:** no established independent air-gap endpoint, no public per-memory signed verifier, and native Memory A2A is absent/unverified or supplied by the framework; all-path semantic governance/complete forensic capture is unverified. Their managed enterprise identity/KMS is stronger in documented scope.
- **Palantir:** the cryptographic memory-attestation column is UNVERIFIED; A2A is PARTIAL/VIA-FRAMEWORK. Published enterprise audit and private deployment do not establish a signed per-memory verifier or universal model-failure closure.
- **Legion:** native coordination and ordinary audit capture are PARTIAL; cryptographic memory attestation is UNVERIFIED. TLS and AES-256 receive documentary Y, while customer KMS custody and universal failure semantics remain unverified. Private delivery does not establish complete cryptographic capture or independently interoperable memory peers.
- **H2O.ai:** transit defaults, per-memory at-rest/KMS coverage and framework A2A are PARTIAL; cryptographic memory attestation is UNVERIFIED. Its Y enterprise/audit cells document controls, with universal judge failure closure and audit completeness still unverified.
- **C3 AI:** native A2A claims, exact memory transit defaults and per-memory at-rest/KMS coverage are PARTIAL; cryptographic memory attestation is UNVERIFIED. Enterprise audit and customer hosting do not establish those missing contracts.
- **Airia:** ordinary audit tracking is PARTIAL and signed forensic export is UNVERIFIED. A2A, TLS and AES-256 receive documentary Y; customer KMS and policy-outage semantics remain unverified. Gateway/tool audit is not a complete forensic attestation of each memory mutation.
- **Credal:** native internal calls and managed at-rest protection are PARTIAL; customer KMS and a signed memory verifier are UNVERIFIED. Human approval and source ACLs are documented, but the human gate is surface-specific.
- **Vectara:** at-rest coverage, communications and audit tracking are PARTIAL, including documented metadata/key-cache exceptions; cryptographic per-memory attestation remains UNVERIFIED. Private deployment does not remove those exceptions.

The same disqualifying cells are explicit for every other row. A row with UNVERIFIED cannot be promoted to “meets all.” No single generic “enterprise ready” check mark substitutes for these contracts.

#### 3d. Multi-LLM architecture across deployment topologies

The earlier 3×7 vote rejected MULTIMODEL as an ai-memory differentiator: **NO 7/7**. That decision is preserved. mem0, cognee, OpenViking and Haystack offer broader independent per-role/component routing; Hindsight, Graphiti and Honcho add further counterexamples. Multiple task names are not multiple independently configurable model instances. Counts below are **documented functional lower bounds (≥)** unless an exact scoped census exists. The ai-memory 15-task census uses a finer taxonomy than several competitors' family counts; do not rank products by these numbers. Unknown closed internals and screen-only candidates are explicitly UNVERIFIED.

The singleton question covers the **entire enabled role set**, including locally staged weights, runtime/provider dependencies and optional features. Federation requires semantic compatibility of query/document vectors and policy behavior across independently operated peers, not just a clustered database. Fail-closed means refusing the relevant unsafe action on unavailable/invalid/low-confidence model output; retry, heuristic fallback, keeping an old answer, IAM denial and a quality evaluator are different mechanisms.

**Precise ai-memory distinction:** independent embedding configuration, a fixed local neural cross-encoder and a shared primary generation client are usable in the endpoint architecture; the auto-tag path changes a model string on that same endpoint. It is not an independent per-role provider router. The same configuration families extend to server deployments, while backend/frontend and SAL feature differences prevent a claim that all 15 tasks run identically from SQLite singleton to Postgres federation. [src/config/auto_tag_endpoint.rs:65](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/config/auto_tag_endpoint.rs#L65), [src/daemon_runtime.rs:6940](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/daemon_runtime.rs#L6940), [Cargo.toml:312](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/Cargo.toml#L312).

Its federation receiver compares model/prefix fingerprints and dimensions before indexing shipped vectors, falling back toward local re-embedding for foreign spaces; the CLI exposes re-embedding controls. This is concrete cross-peer vector-space handling. The fingerprint is based on a **claimed model identity/prefix scheme**, not a cryptographic attestation of weights or proof that two endpoints using the same name compute identical vectors. It does not make arbitrary latent spaces interchangeable. [src/handlers/federation_receive.rs:2651](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/handlers/federation_receive.rs#L2651), [src/handlers/federation_receive.rs:3028](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/handlers/federation_receive.rs#L3028), [src/embeddings.rs:424](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/embeddings.rs#L424), [src/cli/commands/reembed.rs:85](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/cli/commands/reembed.rs#L85).

**No independent fail-closed decision-model judge is established at this release.** Model proposals are checked by deterministic authority/K9 gates. Synthesis supports BlockWrite and FallThrough; no configured LLM can make synthesis ineligible, and HTTP consolidation has placeholder-summary behavior. These are not equivalent to a separate model vetoing destructive generation at a confidence threshold. The requested decision-seam/client files do not exist at this pin; later judge work and its issues are not imported as shipped features. This directly limits the hypothesis in the task brief. [src/mcp/tools/store/synthesis.rs:274](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/tools/store/synthesis.rs#L274), [src/mcp/tools/store/synthesis.rs:293](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/tools/store/synthesis.rs#L293), [src/mcp/tools/store/synthesis.rs:702](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/tools/store/synthesis.rs#L702), [src/handlers/power_consolidation.rs:100](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/handlers/power_consolidation.rs#L100).

### 4. Binding candidate decisions and all votes

“Overall” is the enterprise/federal procurement judgment, allowing managed memory APIs as agent endpoint memory. It does not require every product to be a laptop daemon. A mandatory disconnected-local constraint can make an otherwise ABOVE cloud product ineligible. Federal EQUAL means no established net directional advantage in this evidence, not that both products hold equal authorizations; ON_PAR means balanced strengths/uncertainty, not experimentally equal quality. DIFFERENT-CATEGORY retains meaningful platforms/frameworks/databases without declaring them technically inferior. Trace's evidence-limited tie is particularly not a validated parity claim.

**Existential decision:** **YES** (YES 3/3).

### 6. Differentiators under adversarial review

**Federation.** Independent memory-peer fan-out, acknowledgments, catch-up and vector-space handling are real ai-memory mechanisms. A quorum acknowledgment is not a distributed atomic commit, and the merge comparator does not prove whole-record convergence for equal-rank/equal-time conflicts. Open pagination/convergence defects reduce readiness. Database clustering, search federation, model federation and tactical mesh are useful competitor capabilities, but not interchangeable mechanisms. The earlier “FEDERATION differentiator” result was NO 6/7, YES 1/7; no uniqueness claim follows here. [src/federation/sync.rs:651](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L651), [src/federation/receive.rs:557](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/receive.rs#L557), [src/models/crdt_merge.rs:311](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/models/crdt_merge.rs#L311).

**Signed audit and forensic attestation.** ai-memory has chained events, signature roles and independent verification paths, plus per-record provenance. This is more substantive than an ordinary request log. It does not prove every successful mutation is captured atomically; the SQLite link path is best-effort, unsigned events exist and file-audit checkpoints are a separate incomplete mechanism. Vestige receipts, ContextLattice anchors, AWS CloudTrail integrity digests and Oracle's optional blockchain tables prevent a defensible exclusivity claim. Oracle's generic database feature is not automatically wired into Agent Memory. The historical AUDIT vote was YES 7/7 for useful differentiation, not monopoly. [src/signed_events.rs:2881](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/signed_events.rs#L2881), [src/storage/mod.rs:10119](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L10119), [src/audit.rs:935](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/audit.rs#L935).[^U05-S][^U06-S][^U16-S][^U20-S]

**Governance and model failure.** Enforce escalates unresolved Ask to Deny, but no matching rule/hook returns Allow, and a namespace SQL-read error can become NoPolicy. Optional stricter posture does not erase the release defects. No independent LLM judge was established. Competitors' deterministic IAM/ABAC, default-deny configurations, human approvals and bound write receipts are relevant strengths even without a memory-specific judge. Conversely, a vendor mentioning a safety model does not prove fail-closed destruction. [src/governance/mod.rs:659](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/mod.rs#L659), [src/governance/mod.rs:682](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/mod.rs#L682), [src/storage/mod.rs:22791](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L22791).[^U03-S][^U49-S][^U52-S][^U55-S]

**rust-a2a and wake.** The native same-host wake plane authenticates enrolled-root delegation and transmits bounded AWH1 metadata after durable inbox insertion. It is an optimization for discovering durable rows, not a general distributed message bus, standard Agent2Agent conformance, guaranteed wake delivery or an agent executor. The historical A2A differentiation vote was YES 7/7; broader-market framework implementations now demonstrate stronger standard protocol/orchestration scope. SQLite-only CLI catch-up and open liveness defects qualify backend/fleet claims. [src/mcp/tools/notify.rs:199](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/tools/notify.rs#L199), [src/wake_hub/delegation_verifier.rs:416](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/wake_hub/delegation_verifier.rs#L416), [src/wake_hub/limits.rs:31](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/wake_hub/limits.rs#L31), [src/cli/wake_listen.rs:256](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/cli/wake_listen.rs#L256).

The supplied **MEASURED** wake artifact reports, for 200 samples each, notify-to-`inbox --wait` exit p50/p95/p99 **44.0/816.3/1017.5 ms** on the loaded `/mnt/t9` plane and **20.2/28.8/34.1 ms** in an NVMe control; post-POST wake/read/exit on the first run was **5.5/9.4/15.3 ms**. Crucially, the binary was fix branch `0e5e8de2b` containing later wake fixes, **not `a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940`**. The benchmark was same-host, one recipient, SQLite; it did not test Postgres, cross-host wakes, fan-out or duplicate-hint frequency. These are externally supplied measurements with stated boundaries, not a reproduced release benchmark and not latency credit for this comparison. Source artifact: `WAKE-LATENCY-MEASURED-tmux22.md`; its benchmark receipt is preserved in the synthesis evidence package.

**Endpoint, self-host and air gap.** ai-memory's default SQLite Rust package is a concrete packaging advantage over cloud-only backends. Pre-staged local models permit offline inference; keyword mode avoids model dependency. Optional Postgres/AGE/pgvector and SAL paths add operational dependencies, and MCP/backend/backup parity is not universal. Vestige, libraries with local inference, and documented enterprise private deployments offer alternatives. No complete network-denial acceptance test was run here. A cloud authorization never automatically authorizes a separately installed air gap. [Cargo.toml:312](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/Cargo.toml#L312), [src/embeddings.rs:1858](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/embeddings.rs#L1858), [src/mcp/mod.rs:1610](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/mcp/mod.rs#L1610).

**Encryption.** HTTP TLS is required and a plaintext listener is refused, a useful default. mTLS remains opt-in (#4003). Record-content encryption uses per-record keys only when enabled; title, tags and metadata are outside that envelope. Native customer KMS/HSM and a FIPS-validated module boundary are not established. Managed competitors' default encryption, KMS, rotation and identity administration can be stronger even when their internal record format is undisclosed. [src/daemon_runtime.rs:6070](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/daemon_runtime.rs#L6070), [src/tls.rs:112](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/tls.rs#L112), [src/encryption/mod.rs:1023](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/encryption/mod.rs#L1023), [src/encryption/mod.rs:1068](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/encryption/mod.rs#L1068).

**Multi-model.** NO 7/7 as a generic differentiator remains correct. The useful ai-memory story is a configurable embedder, local reranking and shared generation integrated with local custody and explicit peer vector-space handling. It is not wider per-role routing or shipped independent destructive judges. The singleton-to-federation architecture is a qualified implementation capability; equal role availability and failure semantics across every frontend/backend are not proved. See §3d.

**NSA CSI coverage.** The precise project control-mapping statement is: **all 10 NSA concerns plus 7 recommendations are mapped to shipped controls; concern (a) is fully covered only in enforce mode with enrolled per-agent keys.** This is a mapping of concerns to controls, not a finding that every default configuration fully mitigates them, an NSA endorsement, a compliance authorization, or a passing conformance test. The rechecked identity gate returns without enforcement with zero enrollment; policy-error, revocation, webhook and audit defects materially limit effective coverage. Message signatures on selected storage/federation/wake paths do not mean every MCP message is signed. [src/handlers/identity_binding.rs:410](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/handlers/identity_binding.rs#L410), [src/identity/replay.rs:96](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/replay.rs#L96), [src/identity/sign.rs:178](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/sign.rs#L178), [src/wake_hub/delegation_verifier.rs:416](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/wake_hub/delegation_verifier.rs#L416).

The count above preserves the project's requested mapping convention; it should not be represented as an independent exhaustive enumeration of every recommendation heading in the NSA publication. The May 2026 CSI also contains operational recommendations on vulnerability tracking and network scanning. Implemented validation, least privilege, replay controls and audit provide mechanisms; operators still own deployment boundaries, model/tool egress, monitoring and patch response. This audit did not test all 17 mapped items end to end. [DOC-LEVEL: NSA CSI, May 2026 v1.0](https://www.nsa.gov/Portals/75/documents/Cybersecurity/CSI_MCP_SECURITY.pdf).

### 7. Gaps ai-memory should close

**Open defects count against current readiness.** The U4 voting snapshot had **133 ga-blocker and 105 found-in-testing issues, 150 distinct open issues**. The U5 read-only refresh found **134 ga-blocker and 106 found-in-testing, 151 distinct open issues**. These are overlapping labels, not 240 separate defects. The changed census does not alter the binding votes. All open items are readiness debt; not every report is a reproduced vulnerability in this exact release, and issue counts cannot fairly estimate comparative defect rates for opaque vendors. The snapshots retain state, labels and issue URLs.

Priority work follows the actual deficiencies:

1. **Close identity/isolation and governance failure paths.** Resolve the reported revoked-key refresh race [#4066](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4066), private-event webhook disclosure [#4069](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4069), policy-read fail-open [#4043](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4043), and wildcard enforcement [#4042](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4042). Test authenticated tenancy and denied operations across HTTP/MCP/CLI/backends. Provide enterprise IdP/SSO, workload identity, rotation/revocation and least-privilege administration with clear enforcement defaults. Enrollment and enforce mode must be demonstrably armed.
2. **Make forensic claims match mutation durability.** Resolve successful mutation without durable audit [#4000](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4000), gap/tail verification [#4021](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4021) / [#4086](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4086), and Postgres witness/backend routing [#4070](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4070). Establish atomic capture, externally anchored tail verification, retention/export and restore tests; distinguish file audit from signed database events.
3. **Finish model-failure and destructive-operation contracts.** Resolve content-free consolidation [#4091](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4091), multi-step partial effects and unavailable-model behavior. If independent judges are a target, implement and test separate configuration, authority, confidence semantics and failure closure before claiming them. Later judge report [#4011](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4011) is landing risk, not a shipped release feature. Expand per-role routing and make unused configuration knobs honest.
4. **Demonstrate federation/backend reliability and wake liveness.** Close cursor/convergence [#4060](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4060) / [#4031](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4031) and wake [#4057](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4057) / [#4058](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4058) issues. Run pinned-release fault, partition/rejoin, model-space-change, recovery and fan-out tests. Publish measured Postgres and disconnected deployment boundaries; do not transfer later-fix latency to the release.
5. **Provide complete key and deployment assurance.** Define protection for metadata/indexes/backups, customer KMS/HSM custody, recovery/rotation and cryptographic-module boundaries. Make mTLS's optional posture explicit. Offer a reproducible air-gap package with staged assets, SBOM/build provenance, upgrade/rollback and a network-denial acceptance test.
6. **Develop a scoped federal path and enterprise support evidence.** Identify the actual system/service boundary, deployment sponsor, control responsibilities and evidence package. Achieved FedRAMP/IL service competitors already lead this axis. A deployment inside an authorized cloud helps composition but does not automatically authorize ai-memory or confer a customer's ATO. No schedule, cost or eventual authorization is guaranteed by this assessment.
7. **Improve ecosystem and comparative evidence.** Framework context providers, standard A2A interoperability where useful, and supported operational integrations can close real DX gaps. Run matched-corpus/model/budget retrieval and lifecycle correctness tests against strong peers. Publish denominators, failure modes and workload limits; company-wide vendor scale and GitHub stars are not matched memory benchmarks.

### 8. Limits, reproducibility and authority

This is a static, public-evidence synthesis of the recorded US-market search and adversarial votes. Closed implementations are **DOC-LEVEL (unverified in code)** throughout. Government records establish documentary scope; vendor pages can be incomplete, inconsistent or newer than an authorized release. No gated SSP/SAR, agency authorization letter, complete cap table, FIPS certificate boundary, full SBOM/transitive license audit or production configuration was inspected. No new exploit, inference run, benchmark, disaster-recovery exercise or fully disconnected installation was executed in U5.

U5 re-read 100+ ai-memory release source files covering 400+ cited anchors through the prescribed interface; it also refreshed identity/funding/decisive federal URLs and checked all 519 immutable file:line links across 348 source files for resolution and line validity. Those mechanical checks supplement the claim-specific inspection; they do not independently prove semantics. Fetch success only proves reachability, not the claim: semantic evidence and its qualifications are retained in the source dossiers and footnotes. Some SEC, IBM, LinkedIn and release pages rejected or timed out on refresh; their assertions retain the earlier documentary evidence and explicit uncertainty. Newly discovered deepset US contracting evidence is recorded rather than hidden. Ownership cells with only profile/location evidence remain UNVERIFIED. Funding flags are a partial public-record screen, not a foreign-control adjudication.

Reproducibility package: `u5-evidence/registry-matrices.json` (one row set for all matrices), `input-extracts.json`, `ai-release-recheck.json`, `doc-refresh.json`, `issues-ga-blocker.jsonl`, `issues-found-in-testing.jsonl`, `issue-counts.json`, source-anchor check results, input hashes and structural validation. The three sweep files, D0/D0b/D0c, D1–D9, U1 dossiers, U2/U3/U4 reports, and prior 3×7/OpenViking tallies are input provenance, not substitutes for immutable code or official URLs. This standalone document carries its decisions and supporting source links; internal artifacts provide the longer chain of custody.

Search completeness is time-bounded to the 2026-09-27 research record. Service features, ownership, corporate offices, funding, authorization boundaries and issue states can change. Broad sweep claims of ai-memory exclusivity were rejected where the deeper evidence contradicted them. No row asserts that an unverified capability is absent solely because a closed implementation is unavailable.

**Any REUSE-CODE import or new dependency requires explicit operator authorization per CLAUDE.md §Sole-authority; this assessment authorizes nothing.**

# Part II: ai-memory competitive advantage at code level

## ai-memory competitive advantage: code-level assessment

### 1. Provenance and decision rules

**Assessment date:** 2026-09-27. **Synthesis and live issue refresh:** 2026-09-28 00:17 UTC. **Task:** A10-SYNTH-DOC. **Analyst:** Codex, gpt-6-astra, high reasoning. **Subject:** `alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp`, `release/v1.0.0`; AlphaOne LLC, US (operator-supplied corporate context).

This is the synthesis of a **3x3 adversarial analysis (mine, refute, vote): three mines, three refutations, three votes**. The mining lanes were data/integrity/federation, security/trust/governance, and agents/models/A2A/operations. Refutation covered competitor parity, implementation reality and buyer value. The voters represented federal CISO, enterprise architect and agent-platform CTO concerns. These are three review perspectives from the supplied campaign, not independent laboratory results or three different model vendors.

The code-level advantage that survives is a combination of attributable memory writes, delegated authority, explicit identity continuity/recovery, verifiable evidence and authenticated local wake admission. It is conditional on the specific paths, configuration and custody described below. Generic memory CRUD, provenance fields, temporal retrieval, embeddings, model adapters, MCP, storage adapters and backups have multiple counterparts. No measured performance, retrieval-quality, reliability or cost superiority is established.

**Binding tally:** 182 inventory facets: **84 UNIQUE, 34 RARE, 64 TABLE-STAKES, 0 NOT-REAL**. Value decisions: **45 HIGH, 97 MEDIUM, 39 LOW, 1 NO-CONSENSUS**. **23** facets are both UNIQUE and HIGH. They are not 23 independent advantages: the author-write, subkey, replay and deferred-audit entries repeat across mining lanes. F1-31 remains NO-CONSENSUS on value. Individual-voter prose does not override the tally.

UNIQUE means no functional equivalent was established in the inspected source corpus at the stated boundary. RARE means one or two assessed competitors match that function. TABLE-STAKES means at least three. Neither UNIQUE nor RARE establishes patent novelty, a durable barrier to replication, or absence from uninspected proprietary services. Different cipher choices, wire spelling or enum counts alone do not establish a useful advantage. HIGH is the voters' incremental buyer-value judgment, not release approval. Defaults and defects are separate axes.

**ai-memory source rule.** Implementation and test evidence was obtained only through `codegraph explore "<query>" --path /home/fate_two/v07/v09-dev` and `git -C /mnt/t9/v07/v09-dev show origin/release/v1.0.0:<path>`. CodeGraph is the release-index discovery route; release `git show` is authoritative. The operator identifies the code baseline as `a1403c742`; existing source links use its full commit. Earlier reports observe documentation/tree differences between refs, so this assessment claims equivalence for inspected code, not byte-identical repository trees. Fresh synthesis checks resolved 1,402 implementation/test/config anchors across 245 files with zero line mismatches against the source audit and re-found all 683 cited test-definition occurrences. Repeated test citations are not 683 independent tests. No tests, build, model download, service start or benchmark were run.

**Competitor corpus.** The nine #4055 dossiers are KIP/AndaDB Nexus (D1), mem0 (D2), Ruflo (D3), MemPalace (D4), OpenViking (D5), cognee (D6), agentmemory (D7), TencentDB Agent Memory (D8) and Haystack (D9). The US audit adds the U1 dossiers and sweeps, including Letta Code, Graphiti, Hindsight, Vestige, ContextLattice, Honcho, Memori, MemMachine, Redis Agent Memory, LangGraph/LangMem, Neo4j Agent Memory, SageOx, memsearch, Onyx, Microsoft Agent Framework, Mastra, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Chroma and other inspected candidates. `comp3x7`, `ov3x3`, `us3x3` and the market SWEEP-A/B/C reports are evidence inputs. The complete comparator catalog in §6.4 includes actual source locations and pins; it distinguishes partial counterparts from accepted matches. Fresh read-only hashing matched all 548 local source files referenced by the 238 comparison cards. Closed-service and sweep-only claims do not prove implementation parity or absence. Corporate domicile is context, not a code feature.

**Issue scope.** Fresh read-only queries were `gh issue list --repo alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp --label found-in-testing --state open --limit 250` and the same command with `--label ga-blocker`, adding `--json number,title,body,labels,url`. Results: 109 and 139; 156 distinct reports; neither limit was reached. Membership is unchanged from the latest voter snapshot. Every issue cited as open below is in that union. Some are implementation defects; others are documentation, deployment, review gates or reports on later branches. They are identified as such and do not all falsify the narrow primitive. “None mapped” means no applicable issue identified in these two label sets, not no defects in the repository. Test assertions pin a path or fixture; they do not erase open counterexamples or establish passing CI.

**Artifact authority:** [TALLY.json](TALLY.json), SHA-256 `e397c3ef2104e2ef8f92ca6786334308d57b94e5300fa25547c0b5e8486f6f99`. Supporting synthesis checks: [release anchors and tests](A10-source-verification.json), [competitor source hashes](A10-competitor-source-verification.json), [live found-in-testing issues](A10-open-found-in-testing.json), [live ga-blocker issues](A10-open-ga-blocker.json). Full mechanisms, configuration, tests, comparator evidence and issue titles are reproduced here so this document can be read without the mine/refute/vote narratives.

**Any REUSE-CODE import or new dependency requires explicit operator authorization per CLAUDE.md §Sole-authority; this assessment authorizes nothing.**

<a id="facet-f2-06"></a>
#### 1. F2-06 — Content-bound v1 write attestation with honest trust levels


**Class/value:** UNIQUE (UNIQUE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 3/3). **Code reality:** PARTIAL. **Top-ten selections:** 3/3. **Defect status:** OPEN REPORTS / GATES.

**What it is:** Content-bound v1 write attestation with honest trust levels.

**Implementing symbols:** sign_memory_write [src/identity/attest.rs:471](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/attest.rs#L471); resolve_write_attest_level [src/identity/attest.rs:576](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/attest.rs#L576); persist_write_signature [src/identity/attest.rs:518](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/attest.rs#L518); require_agent_attestation_for [src/identity/attest.rs:196](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/attest.rs#L196); attest_write [src/identity/verify.rs:372](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/verify.rs#L372).

**Mechanism:**

1. Hash content with SHA-256, build SignableWrite from agent, namespace, title, kind, canonical created_at and content hash, then sign its canonical encoding with Ed25519.
2. Resolve the enrolled author key and verify before stamping agent_attested; absent permitted proof becomes claimed. Present forged proof is rejected even in permissive mode, and original write_signature is preserved for later verification.

**Transaction / invariant detail:** The signed structure is `SignableWrite` (`src/identity/sign.rs:381`); `canonical_cbor_write` (`:420`) fixes its encoding and `sign_write` (`:453`) signs it. Stored original author proof and daemon audit evidence are separate objects. The verified tuple excludes tags, priority, valid-time bounds and arbitrary metadata. Signature verification does not encompass the later storage transaction or make all mutations signed.

**Default / activation / configuration:** PARTIAL. AI_MEMORY_REQUIRE_AGENT_ATTESTATION unset: HTTP direct store/bulk/capture require proof; MCP and CLI are permissive. 1 requires it across direct surfaces; 0 opts out. CLI store --sign opts in.

#### 2. F2-22 — Keyless, append-only capability attenuation


**Class/value:** UNIQUE (UNIQUE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 3/3). **Code reality:** REAL-OPT-IN. **Top-ten selections:** 3/3. **Defect status:** No applicable report mapped in the two-label snapshot.

**What it is:** Keyless, append-only capability attenuation.

**Implementing symbols:** attenuate [src/governance/capability.rs:636](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/capability.rs#L636); verify [src/governance/capability.rs:669](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/capability.rs#L669); Caveat::canonical_cbor [src/governance/capability.rs:227](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/capability.rs#L227).

**Mechanism:**

1. A holder serializes one extra caveat, computes HMAC(previous_tag, caveat_bytes), appends the caveat and replaces the tag without the issuer’s private key or root secret.
2. The verifier starts from the root-secret HMAC and folds extensions in order; constant-time tag comparison rejects removal, alteration and reordering. All ancestor constraints still apply.

**Transaction / invariant detail:** `CapabilityToken` holds root caveats, an Ed25519 root signature, ordered extension caveats and the current HMAC tag. `mint_with_secret` (`src/governance/capability.rs:603`) computes `tag0 = HMAC-SHA256(root_secret, canonical_root)`. `attenuate` computes `tagN = HMAC-SHA256(tagN-1, canonical_caveat)` on a clone. `verify` (`:669`; chain fold `:702`) uses the closed configured issuer allowlist, strict root-signature verification and constant-time final-tag comparison. It applies every root and extension caveat conjunctively and clamps authority to the issuer ceiling; the effective caller identity must be supplied by the request wiring. This is a pure token operation, not a database transaction. Retaining a parent token retains that parent authority.

**Default / activation / configuration:** PARTIAL. Verifier enabled by default; requires an explicitly issued token. AI_MEMORY_CAPABILITIES and [capabilities].enabled control participation.

**Pinning tests — source inspected, not executed:** [src/governance/capability.rs:1635](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/capability.rs#L1635)::attenuation_cannot_escalate_and_narrows; [src/governance/capability.rs:1651](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/capability.rs#L1651)::forge_by_removing_a_caveat_breaks_the_chain; [src/governance/capability.rs:1664](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/capability.rs#L1664)::tamper_or_reorder_breaks_chain; [src/governance/capability.rs:1807](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/capability.rs#L1807)::property_verify_accept_implies_request_subset_of_every_ancestor.

**Competitor finding:** 0. No equivalent established at this scope in the assessed source corpus. No equivalent holder-side keyless append-only attenuation established. Central delegation/grant modification is a different operation. Tokens still require an issuer and engaged verification paths. Ruflo also has signed invocation tokens, but their payload binds caller/tool/time/nonce, not call arguments or memory content, and the helper is not a universal dispatcher gate.

**Competitor code evidence:** [K@119](#e-k-119) ([source 1](https://github.com/ldclabs/anda-db/blob/d781b47b646076c3b17a2b20cfc44128f43c8124/rs/anda_cognitive_nexus/src/governance/auth.rs#L20-L50); [source 2](https://github.com/ldclabs/anda-db/blob/d781b47b646076c3b17a2b20cfc44128f43c8124/rs/anda_cognitive_nexus/src/nexus.rs#L8-L19)); [CL@69](#e-cl-69) ([source 1](https://github.com/sheawinkler/ContextLattice/blob/e0daa914fc3f3a9a21363470242ea3fc0bd88964/services/gateway-go/context_passport.go#L442); [source 2](https://github.com/sheawinkler/ContextLattice/blob/e0daa914fc3f3a9a21363470242ea3fc0bd88964/services/gateway-go/context_mesh.go#L789)); [RF@9001](#e-rf-9001) ([source 1](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/d37f283c6e040af9ab12c7e59d2b222a730c9842/v3/@claude-flow/security/src/mcp-caller-identity.ts#L74); [source 2](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/d37f283c6e040af9ab12c7e59d2b222a730c9842/v3/@claude-flow/security/src/mcp-caller-identity.ts#L109)).

**Class/value:** UNIQUE (UNIQUE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 3/3). **Code reality:** REAL-DEFAULT. **Top-ten selections:** 3/3. **Defect status:** No applicable report mapped in the two-label snapshot.

**What it is:** Durable, single-use public-key possession proof.

**Implementing symbols:** PossessionProof::verify_challenge_response [src/identity/pubkey_bind.rs:274](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/pubkey_bind.rs#L274); verify_challenge_response_at [src/identity/pubkey_bind.rs:292](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/pubkey_bind.rs#L292); issue_pubkey_bind_challenge [src/storage/pubkey_history.rs:246](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/pubkey_history.rs#L246); consume_pubkey_bind_challenge [src/storage/pubkey_history.rs:305](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/pubkey_history.rs#L305); bind_agent_pubkey [src/storage/pubkey_history.rs:120](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/pubkey_history.rs#L120).

**Mechanism:**

1. Persist a 32-byte random nonce with agent, canonical candidate key and a 300-second expiry in agent_pubkey_challenges.
2. Consume using conditional UPDATE … consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now; verify_strict checks the candidate’s Ed25519 signature over the domain-separated tuple. A private-field PossessionProof carries exactly that authorized tuple into the storage gate.

**Transaction / invariant detail:** `consume_pubkey_bind_challenge` is a conditional database mutation, not a read-then-write flag. The resulting consumed-challenge carrier is required to construct `PossessionProof`; verification rechecks agent/key equality, `now < expires_at`, and that the expiry is no more than the 300-second issuance window ahead. URL-safe or standard base64 is decoded to a fixed Ed25519 signature and checked with `verify_strict`. Consumption precedes proof validation, so an invalid answer spends the nonce. Binding remains a separate authority decision; this is one-use proof admission, not one transaction guaranteeing enrollment success.

**Default / activation / configuration:** ON. Mandatory for external key binding; no bypass configuration. Enrollment itself is operator initiated.

#### 7. F2-05 — Distinct-guardian threshold identity recovery


**Class/value:** UNIQUE (UNIQUE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 2/3, MEDIUM 1/3). **Code reality:** REAL-OPT-IN. **Top-ten selections:** 2/3. **Defect status:** No applicable report mapped in the two-label snapshot.

**What it is:** Distinct-guardian threshold identity recovery.

**Implementing symbols:** verify_recovery_record [src/identity/lineage.rs:1083](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/lineage.rs#L1083); guardian_set_id_digest [src/identity/lineage.rs:943](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/lineage.rs#L943); enrolled_recovery_guardians [src/identity/lineage.rs:959](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/lineage.rs#L959); recovery_threshold_explicit [src/identity/lineage.rs:992](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/lineage.rs#L992).

**Mechanism:**

1. Recovery records commit to a threshold and guardian-set digest. Decode the versioned quorum, reconstruct the recovery signing input, and verify strict Ed25519 signatures from enrolled guardians.
2. Deduplicate by public-key bytes before counting; reject below the record’s committed threshold. Historical verification reports guardian-set drift rather than silently rewriting the committed threshold from today’s environment.

**Transaction / invariant detail:** `verify_recovery_record` (`src/identity/lineage.rs:1083`) takes the threshold from the signed record, builds a `HashSet<[u8; 32]>` of enrolled guardian keys and a `BTreeSet<[u8; 32]>` of valid distinct signers. Malformed, unenrolled and invalid signatures do not count. It compares the set cardinality against the committed threshold and reports current guardian-set drift separately. The verifier itself is pure; acceptance becomes persistent only through the lineage append path. This is an M-of-N collection of Ed25519 signatures, not Shamir secret sharing or a threshold-signature algorithm.

**Default / activation / configuration:** OPT-IN. AI_MEMORY_RECOVERY_GUARDIAN_PUBKEYS and AI_MEMORY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD; explicit recovery ceremony.

**Pinning tests — source inspected, not executed:** [src/identity/lineage.rs:1846](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/lineage.rs#L1846)::m_of_n_recovery_verifies_to_fresh_head; [src/identity/lineage.rs:1867](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/lineage.rs#L1867)::recovery_verify_uses_committed_threshold_not_env; [src/identity/lineage.rs:1892](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/lineage.rs#L1892)::recovery_duplicate_signer_collapses_to_one; [src/identity/lineage.rs:1947](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/lineage.rs#L1947)::recovery_forged_signature_is_skipped_not_counted.

Generic approvals or cloud IAM recovery are not the same ceremony. Valuable for custody continuity, but it adds operator setup and is not a default feature.

**Mechanism:**

1. Canonicalize rule ID, kind, matcher, severity, reason, namespace, creator and enabled flag; verify_strict checks the operator Ed25519 signature over those bytes.
2. Load enabled rules in ID order, resolve the operator public key, and filter out unsigned or invalidly signed rows when that key is present. Without a resolvable key, legacy unsigned rules still pass.

**Transaction / invariant detail:** The signature gate runs while enabled rules are loaded for evaluation, after canonical field serialization. With an operator key, invalid or unsigned rules are excluded; with no resolvable operator key, the legacy unsigned path remains. **Mechanism:**

1. Assign each refusal occurrence a UUID, serialize a bounded journal frame, fsync a private staging file, publish it under an OS-locked spool and fsync the directory before queue delivery.
2. A supervised drainer serializes occurrence residence checks with signed_events/DLQ insertion; replay acknowledges only durable residence. Quota or journal failure refuses unjournaled admission, preserving distinct identical occurrences without duplicate retries.

**Transaction / invariant detail:** There are two persistence boundaries: filesystem journal admission before a positive submit result, then database signed-event or DLQ residence before journal acknowledgement. The occurrence UUID distinguishes two identical refusals while permitting deduplication of retries of the same occurrence. OS spool locking serializes admission/recovery; the mechanism does not create one atomic transaction spanning filesystem and database. Crash recovery reconciles those stages.

**Default / activation / configuration:** PARTIAL. Installed by daemon boot for wired deferred refusal paths; no universal audit toggle required. Journal-less library queue constructor is still available.

**Implementing symbols:** SignableWrite [src/identity/sign.rs:381](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/sign.rs#L381); canonical_cbor_write [src/identity/sign.rs:420](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/sign.rs#L420); sign_memory_write [src/identity/attest.rs:471](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/attest.rs#L471); resolve_write_attest_level [src/identity/attest.rs:576](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/identity/attest.rs#L576); apply_inbound_write_attestation [src/handlers/federation_receive.rs:954](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/handlers/federation_receive.rs#L954); same-sender/reattribution exceptions [src/handlers/federation_receive.rs:965](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/handlers/federation_receive.rs#L965).

**Mechanism:**

1. sign_memory_write hashes content with SHA-256 and signs canonical CBOR containing a write-domain tag, author, namespace, title, kind and canonical created_at. Ed25519 verification recomputes those bytes against an enrolled author key.
2. Successful verification stamps agent_attested and retains the signature; absent signatures can be claimed only on permissive surfaces. HTTP direct store defaults strict, while ordinary CLI/MCP author-store defaults are permissive; federation write signatures default required.
3. Receive requires a per-write signature for a retained relayed author different from sender; same-sender rows are exempt, and reattributed rows return claimed before that verifier. Thus the default flag does not mean every replicated row is author-attested.

**Default / activation / configuration:** PARTIAL — AI_MEMORY_REQUIRE_AGENT_ATTESTATION: unset is strict on HttpDirect only (src/identity/attest.rs:311). AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_WRITE_SIG defaults true. Set global flag=1 to require signatures on other supporting surfaces. Receive exceptions are implemented at federation_receive.rs:965 and :984.

Ruflo also has signed invocation tokens, but their payload binds caller/tool/time/nonce, not call arguments or memory content, and the helper is not a universal dispatcher gate.

**Class/value:** UNIQUE (UNIQUE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 2/3, MEDIUM 1/3). **Code reality:** PARTIAL. **Top-ten selections:** 0/3. **Defect status:** OPEN REPORTS / GATES.

**What it is:** Verifiable identity-only forget receipts.

**Implementing symbols:** purge_and_tombstone_forget [src/storage/mod.rs:6363](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L6363); forget_tombstone_signable_bytes [src/storage/mod.rs:6494](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L6494); ForgetReceipt [src/storage/mod.rs:6652](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L6652); get_forget_tombstone [src/storage/mod.rs:6695](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L6695); verify_forget_receipt [src/storage/mod.rs:6736](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L6736).

**Mechanism:**

1. The forget transaction inserts one tombstone per victim containing memory ID, namespace, forgotten time, victim owner and optional daemon-key signature. The signable preimage is domain-separated and excludes content or its fingerprint.
2. get_forget_tombstone projects a receipt; verify_forget_receipt recomputes signable bytes and uses Ed25519 verify_strict. It returns Valid, Invalid or Unsigned, so absence of a signature cannot masquerade as verified deletion evidence.

**Transaction / invariant detail:** The tombstone row may retain victim-owner data, but the signed tuple is ID/namespace/time; owner attribution is not covered by that signature. The receipt verifier distinguishes unsigned from valid and invalid evidence. The deletion/tombstone transaction provides a local operation record. It cannot attest destruction of external backups, and #4029 places the inbound tombstone check outside the receive write transaction.

**Default / activation / configuration:** ON — Receipt/tombstone creation is part of forget; cryptographic signature requires an installed daemon audit key. No separate receipt-enable flag; signed=false is possible.

**Pinning tests — source inspected, not executed:** [src/storage/mod.rs:24785](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L24785)::forget_receipt_1832_verify_round_trip; [src/storage/mod.rs:24841](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L24841)::forget_receipt_1832_accessor_projects_tombstone; [tests/erasure_fanout_g30.rs:434](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/erasure_fanout_g30.rs#L434)::forget_tombstone_signable_bytes_deterministic_g30.

No exact signed identity-only forget receipt found. The receipt proves a recorded operation, not erasure of every replica, WAL page or backup.

**Open defects / gates:** [#4029](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4029), [#4067](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4067). Exact titles, labels and scope caveats are in §6.3.

**Release qualification:** Identity-only receipts exist; signatures depend on custody and a receipt cannot prove no stale peer will resurrect the content. Open: #4029, #4067. Issue scope/types are in the facet record.

**Claim boundary:** The signature covers ID/namespace/time, not the victim-owner field, and proves a signer recorded an operation, not independent forensic verification of every copy. Resurrection and undrained peer erasure weaken end-to-end deletion claims.

**Mechanism:**

1. AckTracker records the local commit plus a HashSet of distinct peer acknowledgements, rejects peer-ID drift and enforces a deadline. W is checked against replica count; W=1 is satisfied locally.

**Default / activation / configuration:** OPT-IN — serve --quorum-peers, --quorum-writes and --quorum-timeout-ms. No peers means no distributed acknowledgement benefit; W counts local commit.

**Open defects / gates:** [#3962](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/3962), [#4004](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4004), [#4028](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4028), [#4033](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4033). Exact titles, labels and scope caveats are in §6.3.

**Class/value:** RARE (RARE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 3/3). **Code reality:** REAL-OPT-IN. **Top-ten selections:** 1/3. **Defect status:** No applicable report mapped in the two-label snapshot.

**What it is:** Optional SQLCipher whole-SQLite encryption with fail-closed selection.

**Implementing symbols:** apply_sqlcipher_key [src/storage/connection.rs:1222](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/connection.rs#L1222); refuse_at_rest_requested_without_sqlcipher [src/storage/connection.rs:521](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/connection.rs#L521); set_db_passphrase [src/storage/connection.rs:396](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/connection.rs#L396); build features [Cargo.toml:312](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/Cargo.toml#L312).

Whole-SQLite encryption therefore has a real competitor. **Implementing symbols:** LifecycleState [src/models/memory.rs:340](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/models/memory.rs#L340); can_transition_to [src/models/memory.rs:503](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/models/memory.rs#L503); lifecycle_visible_clause [src/models/memory.rs:580](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/models/memory.rs#L580); set_lifecycle_state [src/storage/mod.rs:3986](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/mod.rs#L3986).

2. set_lifecycle_state reads the old state, checks legality, updates state/time and increments version. lifecycle_visible_clause emits a SQL allowlist shared by read lanes, so an unknown future state is hidden instead of implicitly admitted.

**Default / activation / configuration:** PARTIAL — Default state open; caller lifecycle_state selects ordinary transitions. No enable flag; system-only states are not caller transition targets.

1. VectorClock stores a BTreeMap<peer_id,RFC3339-string>. observe keeps the lexical maximum per peer; merge performs a pointwise union/max, and causality compares both maps with missing entries as the floor.

**Release qualification:** Ordinary inserts stamp the local hostname-derived clock by default; peers are not required for that primitive. Lexical timestamp maxima are diagnostics, not a causal content-merge arbiter; competitor clock/event scopes differ. Open: #4030, #4031, #4060. Issue scope/types are in the facet record.

**Claim boundary:** The vector is diagnostic/preserved state, not the content merge arbiter. It does not fix row-clock regression, per-key non-associativity or a skipped pull page.

#### F1-26 — Signed federation request envelopes and canonical GET authentication


**Class/value:** RARE (RARE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 2/3, MEDIUM 1/3). **Code reality:** REAL-OPT-IN. **Top-ten selections:** 0/3. **Defect status:** OPEN REPORTS / GATES.

**What it is:** Signed federation request envelopes and canonical GET authentication.

**Implementing symbols:** sign_body_with_nonce_header [src/federation/signing.rs:61](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/signing.rs#L61); canonical_get_bytes [src/federation/signing.rs:81](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/signing.rs#L81); verify_header_with_nonce [src/federation/signing.rs:209](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/signing.rs#L209); verify_signature_or_reject [src/handlers/federation_signing_check.rs:2376](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/handlers/federation_signing_check.rs#L2376); verify_get_signature_or_reject [src/handlers/federation_signing_check.rs:2723](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/handlers/federation_signing_check.rs#L2723).

**Mechanism:**

1. POST senders sign exact body bytes, or body plus a domain separator and nonce, using Ed25519; X-Memory-Sig carries the algorithm/base64 signature. The receiver resolves an enrolled peer key and uses verify_strict before applying the envelope.
2. GET pull requests sign canonical method/path/query bytes plus nonce. Peer enrollment is required by default, with explicit unenrolled-peer and signature opt-outs; HTTP success alone is not transport identity proof.

**Default / activation / configuration:** ON — Once federation is configured: AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_SIG=1, AI_MEMORY_FED_REQUIRE_PEER_ENROLLMENT default ON; AI_MEMORY_FED_ALLOW_UNENROLLED_PEERS is an explicit bypass. mTLS is separate and opt-in.

#### F1-49 — Persistent federation DLQ with race-aware replay acknowledgement


**Class/value:** RARE (RARE 2/3, TABLE-STAKES 1/3) · MEDIUM (MEDIUM 3/3). **Code reality:** PARTIAL. **Top-ten selections:** 0/3. **Defect status:** OPEN REPORTS / GATES.

**What it is:** Persistent federation DLQ with race-aware replay acknowledgement.

**Implementing symbols:** FederationDlqSink [src/federation/push_dlq.rs:116](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/push_dlq.rs#L116); replay_once [src/federation/push_dlq.rs:617](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/push_dlq.rs#L617); MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS [src/federation/push_dlq.rs:441](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/push_dlq.rs#L441); land_push_failures [src/federation/sync.rs:563](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L563); success_report_non_ack_reason [src/federation/sync.rs:371](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/federation/sync.rs#L371).

**Mechanism:**

1. Failed fan-out stores per-peer payload/reason/attempt state and coalesces repeated failures under a unique identity. Replay uses bounded/adaptive batches, fresh signed requests and error classes that separate retryable failure from quarantined refusal.
2. A successful replay marks only the payload snapshot it actually sent: a concurrent row refresh fails the acknowledgement CAS and stays pending. Attempts and batch caps bound churn, and quarantined head rows do not starve later work.

**Default / activation / configuration:** OPT-IN — Requires configured federation and persistent DLQ sink/worker. AI_MEMORY_FED_DLQ_REPLAY_MAX_BATCH defaults 2048; inner batch 64; max attempts 100.

**Pinning tests — source inspected, not executed:** [tests/federation_dlq_replay.rs:246](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/federation_dlq_replay.rs#L246)::replay_drains_dlq_when_peer_recovers; [tests/federation_dlq_replay.rs:714](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/federation_dlq_replay.rs#L714)::replay_ack_leaves_row_pending_when_snapshot_is_stale_2360; [tests/federation_dlq_replay.rs:361](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/federation_dlq_replay.rs#L361)::quarantined_head_does_not_starve_take_batch_1578.

**Competitor finding:** 2. OpenViking; SageOx / ox OpenViking RAGFS retry queues and SageOx durable outbox/dedup provide restart-aware retry patterns. The exact payload-snapshot acknowledgement CAS is narrower; these are not universal exactly-once delivery contracts.

**Competitor code evidence:** [OV@127](#e-ov-127) ([source 1](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/blob/a09a9d20a8e07d08973aee177802d00e08df29e6/crates/ragfs/src/core/multibackend_wrapper.rs#L145-L158); [source 2](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/blob/a09a9d20a8e07d08973aee177802d00e08df29e6/crates/ragfs/src/core/multibackend_wrapper.rs#L237-L299)); [OX@61](#e-ox-61) ([source 1](https://github.com/sageox/ox/blob/c7a76abe26e827fd2d3efed0abd82d49853a9782/internal/daemon/murmur_outbox.go#L29); [source 2](https://github.com/sageox/ox/blob/c7a76abe26e827fd2d3efed0abd82d49853a9782/internal/daemon/murmur_relay.go#L54)).

**Open defects / gates:** [#4033](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4033), [#4035](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4035), [#4067](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4067). Exact titles, labels and scope caveats are in §6.3.

**Release qualification:** The persistent DLQ is useful but optional; unbounded responses, destructive redelivery snapshots and worker scheduling prevent reliable end-to-end replay claims. Open: #4033, #4035, #4067. Issue scope/types are in the facet record.

**Claim boundary:** Outbound peer response bodies are unbounded (#4033). Replay transport can be reliable while the repeated merge destroys a recovery snapshot (#4035). DLQ is neither consensus nor an infinite-retention delivery promise.

**Issue applicability:** [#4033](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4033) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4035](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4035) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4067](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4067) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]. Exact current titles appear in §6.3.

**Mechanism:**

1. SignedEvent holds payload hash, actor, type, attestation level, timestamp, sequence, predecessor hash and optional cause hash. append_signed_event_no_tx reads the prior canonical-row SHA-256, assigns the next sequence and binds daemon-signed rows to their final row context before insert.
2. Callers such as operator dequarantine, crypto erase and swarm rewind invoke it inside their mutation transaction. verify_chain checks sequence, predecessor linkage and row-signature classifications; unsigned is a distinct level rather than a valid missing signature.

**Default / activation / configuration:** ON — Chain append on wired operations; daemon key required for daemon_signed, otherwise explicit unsigned posture. No claim that every write has a transactional event.

**Mechanism:**

1. check runs PRAGMA integrity_check and refuses a non-ok verdict. If sqlite_master includes a root-less view/virtual table, it additionally counts reachable dbstat pages, freelist pages, auto-vacuum pointer-map pages and the reserved pending-byte page, requiring their sum to equal page_count.
2. The backup staging verifier and recovery integrity_verdict reuse this routine and propagate unavailable/error results. A separate FTS integrity command exists, but its present SQL does not compare external-content rows with the index.

**Default / activation / configuration:** ON — Automatic inside the invoked backup staging/recovery integrity paths; no feature flag for page accounting. This is not an always-running database integrity scan. FTS deep checking is a separate requested diagnostic.

**Competitor finding:** 1. Ruflo (Claude Flow) Ruflo validates SQLite backup integrity before recovery. ai-memory's extra page census is narrower protection; PRAGMA-based structural validation is not unique and does not authenticate content or establish FTS agreement.

**Competitor code evidence:** [RF@129](#e-rf-129) ([source 1](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/d37f283c6e040af9ab12c7e59d2b222a730c9842/v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/memory-backup.ts#L41-L59); [source 2](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo/blob/d37f283c6e040af9ab12c7e59d2b222a730c9842/v3/@claude-flow/cli/src/services/memory-backup.ts#L50-L112)).

**Open defects / gates:** [#4036](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4036). Exact titles, labels and scope caveats are in §6.3.

**Release qualification:** Whole-file checks run in invoked backup/recovery paths. The separate FTS defect does not refute page accounting; neither establishes semantic correctness. Open: #4036. Issue scope/types are in the facet record.

**Claim boundary:** Structural page accounting does not authenticate memory contents or prove semantic-index agreement. #4036 specifically concerns the separate FTS command omitting rank=1; it is not evidence that this whole-file page census is defective. PostgreSQL has no equivalent SQLite page census.

**Issue applicability:** [#4036](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4036) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]. Exact current titles appear in §6.3.
