#### F2-26 — Transactionally sequenced database audit hash chain


**Class/value:** RARE (RARE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 2/3, MEDIUM 1/3). **Code reality:** PARTIAL. **Top-ten selections:** 0/3. **Defect status:** OPEN REPORTS / GATES.

**What it is:** Transactionally sequenced database audit hash chain.

**Implementing symbols:** canonical_chain_bytes [src/signed_events.rs:677](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/signed_events.rs#L677); append_signed_event [src/signed_events.rs:2881](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/signed_events.rs#L2881); append_signed_event_no_tx [src/signed_events.rs:2931](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/signed_events.rs#L2931); verify_chain [src/signed_events.rs:1338](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/signed_events.rs#L1338).

**Mechanism:**

1. Read the highest sequence and SHA-256 of that row’s canonical, length-prefixed bytes; assign next sequence and prev_hash at the append funnel, ignoring caller-supplied chain coordinates.
2. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes SQLite head allocation and INSERT, with a UNIQUE sequence constraint as backup. The no_tx variant composes with a caller-owned data transaction; verification walks ordered rows and checks contiguity plus predecessor hashes.

**Default / activation / configuration:** ON. No hash-chain toggle for signed_events; events may be unsigned if signing custody is absent. Caller must use the transactional append funnel.

**Pinning tests — source inspected, not executed:** [tests/verify_audit_trail_pe8.rs:129](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/verify_audit_trail_pe8.rs#L129)::deleted_middle_row_surfaces_sequence_gap; [tests/verify_audit_trail_pe8.rs:91](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/verify_audit_trail_pe8.rs#L91)::content_tamper_breaks_chain_at_next_row; [src/signed_events.rs:3589](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/signed_events.rs#L3589)::issue_1930_length_prefix_defeats_separator_collision; [src/signed_events.rs:4140](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/signed_events.rs#L4140)::append_signed_event_refuses_when_null_sequence_present.

**Competitor finding:** 2. Vestige; Cognee Vestige atomically advances signed receipt chains; Cognee serializes transactional provenance sequence allocation with locks. Hash-chained database audit is shared; Cognee is unsigned/default-off and captures best-effort provenance.

**Competitor code evidence:** [V@83](#e-v-83) ([source 1](https://github.com/samvallad33/vestige/blob/9cb6f9c292c95bf1ca385ed04f1641736d24129f/crates/vestige-core/src/storage/receipt_attestation.rs#L1-L39); [source 2](https://github.com/samvallad33/vestige/blob/9cb6f9c292c95bf1ca385ed04f1641736d24129f/crates/vestige-core/src/storage/attestation_store.rs#L414-L538)); [COG@140](#e-cog-140) ([source 1](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee/blob/eb90d03740755f5252b8b12cce91fd09970f2d81/cognee/modules/provenance/integrity.py#L34-L75); [source 2](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee/blob/eb90d03740755f5252b8b12cce91fd09970f2d81/cognee/modules/provenance/integrity.py#L104-L125)).

**Release qualification:** Transactional chain sequence allocation is real; missing events and nontransactional caller behavior still defeat complete-audit claims. Open: #3660, #4000. Issue scope/types are in the facet record.

**Claim boundary:** Chain integrity for rows present is not proof that every successful operation emitted a row. Plain SHA-256 links alone cannot defeat an attacker rewriting the entire chain.

**Implementing symbols:** ForensicDecision [src/governance/audit.rs:80](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/audit.rs#L80); append_row [src/governance/audit.rs:1109](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/audit.rs#L1109); run_writer [src/governance/audit.rs:204](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/audit.rs#L204); read_chain_tail [src/governance/audit.rs:1237](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/audit.rs#L1237); verify_since [src/governance/audit.rs:1398](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/governance/audit.rs#L1398).

**Mechanism:**

1. Build typed forensic decision rows with prior-row hash; Ed25519-sign canonical row bytes when a signing key is installed, compute the row hash, and serialize to dated forensic JSONL files.

**Class/value:** RARE (RARE 3/3) · HIGH (HIGH 2/3, MEDIUM 1/3). **Code reality:** PARTIAL. **Top-ten selections:** 0/3. **Defect status:** OPEN REPORTS / GATES.

**What it is:** Fresh per-record DEKs and content-only storage sealing.

**Implementing symbols:** seal_content [src/encryption/mod.rs:1106](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/encryption/mod.rs#L1106); seal_content_per_record [src/encryption/mod.rs:1130](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/encryption/mod.rs#L1130); open_content [src/encryption/mod.rs:1213](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/encryption/mod.rs#L1213); open_content_per_record [src/encryption/mod.rs:1233](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/encryption/mod.rs#L1233); encryption_enabled [src/encryption/mod.rs:1054](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/encryption/mod.rs#L1054).

**Mechanism:**

1. Draw a random 32-byte DEK per record, encrypt content with ChaCha20-Poly1305 and a separate random nonce, then wrap the DEK using the X25519 envelope scheme.
2. Store version 0x03, wrapped-key length/key, nonce and ciphertext in encrypted_envelope; leave content as an empty placeholder. Reads key off envelope presence, so disabling future encryption does not make existing ciphertext unreadable.

**Default / activation / configuration:** OPT-IN. AI_MEMORY_ENCRYPT_AT_REST=1 or [encryption].at_rest=true; default off. Missing agent identity or sealing failure refuses instead of storing plaintext.

**Pinning tests — source inspected, not executed:** [tests/encryption_at_rest.rs:391](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/encryption_at_rest.rs#L391)::commit_b_on_path_seals_content_and_get_decrypts; [tests/encryption_at_rest.rs:427](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/encryption_at_rest.rs#L427)::commit_b_off_path_is_byte_identical; [tests/encryption_at_rest.rs:521](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/tests/encryption_at_rest.rs#L521)::commit_b_toggle_off_still_reads_encrypted_rows; [src/encryption/mod.rs:1587](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/encryption/mod.rs#L1587)::per_record_envelope_round_trips_via_open_content.

**Competitor finding:** 1. OpenViking OpenViking draws random per-file keys, AES-GCM encrypts content and wraps keys through local/Vault/KMS providers. That is functional per-object DEK envelope parity; file versus row granularity and cipher suite differ. Neither encrypts every index/metadata copy automatically.

**Competitor code evidence:** [OV@97](#e-ov-97) ([source 1](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/blob/a09a9d20a8e07d08973aee177802d00e08df29e6/openviking/crypto/config.py#L32-L54); [source 2](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/blob/a09a9d20a8e07d08973aee177802d00e08df29e6/openviking/crypto/config.py#L63-L75)).

**Release qualification:** Fresh record DEKs seal content only and are off by default. Peer plaintext residency and recovery parity limit the full custody claim; OpenViking's envelope scope differs. Open: #3928, #3961. Issue scope/types are in the facet record.

**Claim boundary:** Only content is sealed: titles, tags, metadata and other representations are not covered by this envelope. Federation obtains plaintext for authorized application transport; this is not peer-blind end-to-end encryption.

**Claim boundary:** Heavily qualified integration surface: subscriber visibility leakage, wrong implicit HTTPS port, duplicate correlation_id, Unicode validator panic, PG counters/unsubscribe residue, queued-work loss and dispatcher stalls are open. **Issue applicability:** [#3745](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/3745) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#3979](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/3979) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4069](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4069) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4074](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4074) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4075](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4075) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4076](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4076) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4079](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4079) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4081](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4081) [IMPLEMENTATION-REPORT]; [#4083](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4083) [DOC/CLAIM]. ### 5. NOT-REAL / downgraded claims

**No one of the 182 inventoried mechanisms is wholly unimplemented.** The binding tally therefore has zero NOT-REAL facets. This does not validate the broader claims below. Missing features receive no extra facet, and a real primitive with a defeated end-to-end guarantee stays qualified.

| Claim rejected or narrowed | Code-level reason and disposition |
|---|---|
| “Convergent memory CRDT; lossless multi-master merge.” | [F1-18](#facet-f1-18)/[F1-19](#facet-f1-19): scalar max is not a PN-counter; tag union lacks observed-remove state. Timestamp choice and metadata inheritance produce order-dependent results (#4030, #4031); merged state can exceed receive limits (#4032). Both remain UNIQUE/LOW at their narrow implementation boundaries. |
| “Quorum means consensus, atomic fleet commit or no partial writes.” | [F1-50](#facet-f1-50): counts acknowledgements, exposes partial success and does not roll back local/remote commits. RARE/MEDIUM; OpenViking has a native acknowledgement counterpart. |
| “Catch-up cannot miss records.” | [F1-51](#facet-f1-51): explicit null and absent progress watermarks collapse in pullers, skipping tied full pages (#4060). Authentication and response bounds do not prove eventual convergence. UNIQUE/LOW. |
| “Signed inbound content cannot dequarantine the wrong state.” | [F1-22](#facet-f1-22), [F1-31](#facet-f1-31), [F1-32](#facet-f1-32): author signatures exist, but cross-ID and same-ID release decisions have #3901/#4017. Quarantine is opt-in and a case-sensitive parser disagrees with the hardened-profile floor (#3619). Value of F1-31 is NO-CONSENSUS. |
| “Forget proves all copies are irrecoverable.” | [F1-45](#facet-f1-45) through [F1-48](#facet-f1-48): signed receipts record an operation, not destruction of backups. Tombstone check outside receive serialization permits resurrection (#4029); zero catch-up interval can strand erasure outbox work (#4067). Content DEK destruction is conditional on sealed records and retained custody. |
| “Every action/read is durably audited; rollback is impossible.” | [F2-26](#facet-f2-26), [F2-32](#facet-f2-32), [F3-51](#facet-f3-51): cryptographic chain integrity is not event completeness. Engaged read audit can be lost (#3660), successful links can lack append evidence (#4000), and final PostgreSQL witness/shutdown paths have #4070/#4072. Journal guarantees cover admitted deferred occurrences only. |
| “Flat JSONL audit emits periodic signed CHECKPOINT.sig anchors.” | [F2-34](#facet-f2-34)/[F3-50](#facet-f3-50): the flat file uses an unsigned hash chain and no checkpoint emission loop. Separate database signed events and forensic signed files are real; the missing emitter gets no facet. |
| “The LLM independently judges destructive consolidation.” | [F3-22](#facet-f3-22)/[F3-24](#facet-f3-24): fixed similarity thresholds admit merge; the LLM supplies summary text (#3807). Empty output and stale source snapshots are accepted (#4046/#4045). Compactor verification is a successful read, not semantic equivalence. |
| “Independent configured [decision] provider / destructive neural judge ships.” | [F3-30](#facet-f3-30): synthesis and structured candidate verdicts use implemented generative pathways; the separate [decision] provider is open scope #3806. No extra feature or independent-model assurance is credited. Recorder/judge/stopper cryptographic roles are not three neural models. |
| “GPU inference/backend is implemented.” | The inspected model paths in [F3-13](#facet-f3-13), [F3-15](#facet-f3-15), [F3-17](#facet-f3-17) do not establish a shipped GPU backend. No GPU-performance or execution advantage is credited. |
| “Private-by-default means complete tenant isolation or no private replication.” | [F2-13](#facet-f2-13) and [F2-16](#facet-f2-16): request visibility, authenticated principal binding, ownership and peer residency are distinct. Permissive caller contexts and reported read/event paths prevent a universal ACL claim. |
| “Default air gap or internal-CIDR-only inference.” | [F2-44](#facet-f2-44)/[F3-19](#facet-f3-19): this release has Allow/LoopbackOnly/Deny, not the later internal-only implementation. First-run model fetching exists (#3991); doctor/reembed have source-visible gate gaps (#4121/#4122). #4123 is an open download-scope ruling, not proof that weight fetching uploads memory. |
| “Certificate pins add full CA/expiry/hostname validation.” | [F2-49](#facet-f2-49): custom leaf-fingerprint trust is an alternate trust mode. It checks the accepted leaf and handshake key possession; it does not independently perform all conventional CA/name/expiry checks. |
| “Memory signature proves content truth, model identity or hardware custody.” | [F2-06](#facet-f2-06)/[F2-08](#facet-f2-08): Ed25519 proves control of the enrolled signer over a bounded payload. Model-version strings are signed claims; mutable metadata is outside v1. HSM/TPM custody is not established. |
| “Wake A2A is Google A2A interoperability or guaranteed remote task execution.” | [F3-03](#facet-f3-03)/[F3-04](#facet-f3-04): implemented protocol is same-host UDS metadata notification with delegated admission. Bounded lossy wake transport points to durable rows; it is not a remote standardized task protocol. #3637 remains a security-review gate; #4057/#4120 affect startup. |
| “PostgreSQL and SQLite have complete feature and lifecycle parity.” | [F1-52](#facet-f1-52)/[F3-45](#facet-f3-45): explicit unsupported adapter behavior, backend gates and the listed witness/shutdown/graph defects refute blanket parity. SAL is a typed interface, not a parity proof. |
| “Signed rules guarantee fail-closed policy execution.” | [F2-36](#facet-f2-36): no resolvable operator key retains legacy acceptance; an invalid signed rule is skipped. Matcher and version-capture defects #4042/#4044 remain. Rule authenticity does not repair policy evaluation or make missing policy deny all. |
| “US company + cryptography implies federal authorization, FIPS validation or NSA certification.” | Domicile is supplied context. No authorization/certification or validated-module evidence is established by the inspected code. The implementation is not a compliance determination. |

Narrow UNIQUE combinations also receive LOW or MEDIUM value where utility is limited or repeated: fixed genesis CIDs, merge details, wire batch ordering, literal named profiles, erasure intent without working fleet completion, signed skills without demonstrated buyer displacement, and schema/projection bookkeeping. The full register preserves these decisions instead of presenting every unique implementation choice as a high-value advantage.

### 7. How to present these truthfully

Use a bounded claim: **“In the inspected release and competitor source corpus, ai-memory combines content-bound author-write proofs, holder-attenuable delegation, explicit identity succession/recovery and authenticated local wake admission. Activation and defect limits apply per mechanism.”** Do not replace “inspected corpus” with “the market,” or “implemented” with “validated in production.”

State defaults per surface. HTTP direct signed-write admission is stricter by default than MCP/CLI. Capability verification defaults on but usable tokens/issuers require provisioning. Lineage, guardian recovery, certified instance writes, wake wiring, operator-signed rules, independent audit roles, SQLCipher and content sealing each require the stated activation. Do not collapse those conditions into “secure by default.”

Treat tests as source evidence unless an actual run is cited. Describe audit signatures as authenticity/integrity evidence for captured events, receipts as operation evidence, and model references as claims. Do not say that signatures prove truth, complete capture, all-copy destruction, runtime model measurement or regulator approval. Publish known defects beside any dependent claim.

Count overlapping mechanisms once when positioning the product. F1-22/F2-06 are author attribution; F1-24/F2-08 are certified subkeys; F1-25/F2-07 are fresh-write replay; F2-32/F3-56 are deferred audit. F1-55, F2-26–35 and F3-51 share audit machinery. F1-45–48 overlap F2-55–57 erasure; F2-40/F3-57 share approval quorum; F2-58/F3-59 share record-stop. The wake wire/admission/revalidation/forwarder compose one optional local coordination subsystem. Facet totals are an inventory, not an additive moat score.

The following claim register applies the named activation and defect qualification from each linked facet. “Supports” is deliberately limited to the implemented operation; “Does not support” states the relevant ceiling, not a promise of a future fix.

| Facet | Claim supported, with stated activation/defects | Claim not supported / necessary limitation |
|---|---|---|
| [F1-01](#facet-f1-01) | Implements “Fifteen typed memory kinds in one persistent record”; TABLE-STAKES/LOW in this corpus. | Types classify records; they do not prove a claim true or an instruction authoritative. Test pins cover persistence/defaults and kind adoption, not epistemic correctness. |
| [F1-02](#facet-f1-02) | Implements “Enforced lifecycle transitions and shared hidden-state filtering”; RARE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | Local transition validation does not make a content-plus-lifecycle request atomic. Federation lifecycle is LWW, not a monotone containment lattice. |
| [F1-03](#facet-f1-03) | Implements “Structured source provenance and evidence filters”; TABLE-STAKES/HIGH in this corpus. | Caller-supplied provenance is not external-source verification. Same-ID merge optional fields can become order-dependent (#4031). |
| [F1-04](#facet-f1-04) | Implements “Kind and confidence provenance retention on title-slot upsert”; UNIQUE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | These pins concern SQL title-slot upserts. Do not transfer the guarantee to all same-ID CRDT merges: merge_memory separately chooses max confidence and LWW confidence_source. Kind provenance is outside the signed write envelope. |
| [F1-05](#facet-f1-05) | Implements “Claim valid-time intervals independent of write timestamps”; TABLE-STAKES/HIGH in this corpus. | This is claim-validity support plus write timestamps, not complete system-versioned bitemporal history or transaction-time as-of reconstruction. Bounds are unsigned caller assertions. |
| [F1-06](#facet-f1-06) | Implements “Signed temporal graph edges and invalidation”; UNIQUE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | Relational temporal edges are implemented. PostgreSQL AGE can expose rejected duplicate-payload validity or stale projected results; do not claim identical temporal results on every graph path. |
| [F1-07](#facet-f1-07) | Implements “Stable content-addressed genesis identity beside mutable UUID records”; UNIQUE/LOW in this corpus. | An unkeyed hash detects inconsistency, not a coherent rewrite by a database attacker. cid_genesis contains identity fields and a content digest; erasure must scrub it. Legacy unverifiable rows can have NULL cid. |
| [F1-08](#facet-f1-08) | Implements “Bounded derivation DAG with cycle refusal and retained ancestor identifiers”; UNIQUE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | This is bounded provenance reachability, not unlimited transitive closure. PostgreSQL deferred mode uses relational CTE; sync AGE can still miss an edge queued after a projection failure. |
| [F1-09](#facet-f1-09) | Implements “Transactional consolidation with retained source tombstones”; UNIQUE/LOW in this corpus. | Database atomicity does not establish semantic preservation: placeholder/empty summaries and stale source snapshots are open defects. | [F1-10](#facet-f1-10) | Implements “Optional identity-only revision chain”; UNIQUE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | This records that a revision occurred; it cannot recover erased prior text. The archive snapshot mechanism has separate PostgreSQL absence and SQLite replay-replacement defects. |
| [F1-11](#facet-f1-11) | Implements “Derived-memory contamination with preserved prior lifecycle”; RARE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | The inspected release has SQLite production stamping, not blanket PostgreSQL stamping. Prior-state metadata is not evidence of an implemented automatic restoration operation. #3946/#4010 concern later PG containment work reported in the open issue set. The supersedes hook logs a stamping failure and continues (src/mcp/tools/link.rs:463), so successful link creation is not an atomic guarantee of completed descendant containment. |
| [F1-12](#facet-f1-12) | Implements “Explicit swarm containment with dry-run and routine freeze”; UNIQUE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | “Rewind” is containment and freezing, not reverse execution of external actions or restoration of earlier text. The inspected implementation is SQLite; the PG CLI sidecar problem is open. |

| [F3-45](#facet-f3-45) | Implements “Async Postgres adapter with pgvector and optional AGE projection”; TABLE-STAKES/MEDIUM in this corpus. | Topology choice is real, not transparent parity. Pool size 1 bootstrap can deadlock (#4041); stale/pending AGE can omit edges (#3887/#3946) and projection races are reported (#4039/#4038). Lifecycle/content atomicity and ranking also differ. Live PG tests require an external test database. |
| [F3-46](#facet-f3-46) | Implements “Application-level peer replication with quorum writes and catch-up”; UNIQUE/LOW in this corpus. | A credible topology differentiator with substantial correctness qualifications: cursor skips, order-dependent merge, stale resurrection/scope races, lease/transition failures and unbounded push-response reads are open. mTLS is opt-in (#4003); local quorum counting and private-row peer custody must be disclosed. |
| [F3-47](#facet-f3-47) | Implements “Declared deployment shapes and transport security floors”; UNIQUE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | Shapes tie configuration together; they do not deploy an enterprise topology or confer certification. #3709 remains an open umbrella despite TLS code, #3619 reports a floor/live-reader token mismatch, #4006 stale help, #4003 mTLS overclaim and #4077 a destructive documented deployment recipe. |
| [F3-48](#facet-f3-48) | Implements “Background maintenance and staged HTTP shutdown”; TABLE-STAKES/LOW in this corpus. | #4072 SIGTERM bypasses drain; #4070 final witness targets SQLite sidecar on Postgres; #4062 detached atomiser can still write. #4037 concerns Postgres GC archive/delete snapshot drift. “Every writer stopped and every backend witnessed” is not a supportable guarantee. |
| [F3-49](#facet-f3-49) | Implements “Prometheus metrics and scoped monitoring credentials”; TABLE-STAKES/MEDIUM in this corpus. | #4068: monitoring authentication failures bypass shared backoff. #4081: Postgres subscription counters are hardcoded zero and updates hit SQLite. Exposed counters are only as complete as their writers; they are not measured competitor-performance evidence. |
| [F3-50](#facet-f3-50) | Implements “Operational logging and optional chained JSON audit file”; TABLE-STAKES/LOW in this corpus. | Open reports cover silent sink degradation, secret-valued SQLx query parameters, logged titles, undetected sequence gaps/tail loss and flaky tracing assertions. Syslog’s helper refusal does not prove main refuses boot. No complete, lossless observability claim is justified. |
| [F3-51](#facet-f3-51) | Implements “Database signed events and independent governance role anchors”; UNIQUE/HIGH in this corpus. | #4000 successful SQLite link creation can lack append evidence; #3660 engaged read audit loss; #4044 policy version fetched after evaluation; #4070 Postgres final witness omission. Cryptographic tamper evidence does not establish complete event capture or correct policy attribution. |
| [F3-52](#facet-f3-52) | Implements “Deterministic namespace/operation permission pipeline”; TABLE-STAKES/LOW in this corpus. | The live default is enforce despite the enum’s serde Default being advisory. #4042 mixed **/* matching can skip a configured deny; #4043 namespace-policy read errors become NoPolicy. Enforce without applicable policy is not default-deny. |
| [F3-53](#facet-f3-53) | Implements “Executable and persistent hook chains with ordered decisions”; TABLE-STAKES/MEDIUM in this corpus. | A genuine policy-extension seam that could call an external model or service. No enrolled hook means no such judge, and optional external execution is not a shipped independent destructive_judge implementation. |
| [F3-54](#facet-f3-54) | Implements “Mandatory hook presence and enforced fail-closed execution”; TABLE-STAKES/HIGH in this corpus. | This is an implemented deterministic enforcement seam with explicit activation. It can make absence of a configured external judge blocking; it cannot establish the correctness of that judge’s answer. |
| [F3-55](#facet-f3-55) | Implements “Typed agent-action governance and versioned verdict evidence”; TABLE-STAKES/MEDIUM in this corpus. | #4044 can sign a policy version that did not evaluate the action; #3660 limits durable read-decision evidence; #4042 affects glob matching. The substrate checks its wired actions, not every arbitrary action an external agent could execute. |
| [F3-56](#facet-f3-56) | Implements “Durably admitted deferred governance audit with replay and DLQ”; UNIQUE/HIGH in this corpus. | Strong admission/recovery mechanism for its specific blocking-verdict path. #3660 means it must not be generalized to every engaged read decision; shutdown/backend defects remain relevant to final audit certification. |
| [F3-57](#facet-f3-57) | Implements “Human approval transport and distinct-signer quorum”; UNIQUE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | #4025 reports approval committed before action execution, making failed/lost execution nonretryable. #4073 is stale HMAC/SSE documentation. Approval authenticity does not give atomic exactly-once execution of the approved action. |
| [F3-58](#facet-f3-58) | Implements “Signed webhooks with bounded retry, replay and dead-letter inspection”; RARE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | Heavily qualified integration surface: subscriber visibility leakage, wrong implicit HTTPS port, duplicate correlation_id, Unicode validator panic, PG counters/unsubscribe residue, queued-work loss and dispatcher stalls are open. Do not advertise lossless fan-out or raw-body HMAC semantics. |
| [F3-59](#facet-f3-59) | Implements “Persistent record-stop fence for mutation suspension”; UNIQUE/MEDIUM in this corpus. | An operator kill switch for instrumented substrate writes, not a proof every mutation is fenced. Open read-only-tool side effects and structural scanner blind spots reduce coverage assurance; C8 findings concern bypass detection, not automatically a reproduced exploit of every stop path. |
| [F3-60](#facet-f3-60) | Implements “Durable action frontier, leases and frozen routine definitions”; TABLE-STAKES/MEDIUM in this corpus. | Useful durable coordination, not a complete autonomous scheduler or tool-execution runtime. Lease-read errors can fail open (#3986), expired leases can block federation transitions (#3729), and nonce-before-CAS receive can drop transitions (#4024). |
| [F3-61](#facet-f3-61) | Implements “SQLite backup manifests and staged verified restore”; TABLE-STAKES/HIGH in this corpus. | A concrete recovery workflow, not cross-backend backup parity. #4080 can point shipped backup timers at the wrong store; #4077 concerns a deployment recipe deleting independent keys/audit/TLS volumes, which a database-only snapshot cannot restore. |
| [F3-62](#facet-f3-62) | Implements “Audited transcript-derived memory-kind refinement”; TABLE-STAKES/LOW in this corpus. | This refines stored type metadata; it does not validate factual truth or introduce a separately routed classifier model. Reclassified rows are skipped on rerun, but unchanged Observation candidates remain eligible. The bounded list is fetched before the Observation filter, so eventual progress through every candidate is not established by the budget alone. No directly matching open issue appeared in the two requested label snapshots. |

### III.1 — Canonical North Star and secondary anchor

The operator-designated authority is [the landing page, “The standard”](https://alphaonedev.github.io/ai-memory-mcp/), retrieved for this review. Verbatim standard:

> **One North Star: mission-critical.**
>
> Every gate, issue, and test is measured against one bar — that a Fortune 500 or a government could trust it with mission-critical work.
>
> **Data integrity** — No silent loss; no partial or unsigned commit.
>
> **Security** — Operator rules never bypassed; no fail-open.
>
> **Performance** — Bounded, non-DoS-able, live under contention.
>
> **Reliability** — Cross-backend parity, recoverability, no kill-switch.

| Pillar | Binding criterion IDs |
|---|---|
| DATA INTEGRITY | **DI1** no silent loss; **DI2** no partial commit; **DI3** no unsigned commit |
| SECURITY | **SE1** operator rules never bypassed; **SE2** no fail-open |
| PERFORMANCE | **PF1** bounded; **PF2** non-DoS-able; **PF3** live under contention |
| RELIABILITY | **RL1** cross-backend parity; **RL2** recoverability; **RL3** no kill-switch |
| Co-ranked mandate | **EN1** only encrypted data in transit anywhere in the ecosystem |

EN1 ranks with the North Star. The security document states: “only encrypted data in transit. there is to never be any unencrypted data in transit anywhere in the ai-memory architecture.” It expressly excludes exemptions for loopback, localhost, development, single-node or lab configurations. Transport authentication, content-free frames and local peer credentials do not themselves encrypt bytes. [docs/SECURITY.md:194](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/SECURITY.md#L194)

| Secondary ID | Moonshot property | Source |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Endpoint-resident | [docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md:51](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md#L51) (§2.1) |
| M2 | Coherent across sessions and model generations | [docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md:61](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md#L61) (§2.2) |
| M3 | Stoppable without silent corruption | [docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md:71](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md#L71) (§2.3) |
| M4 | Improvable across model generations | [docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md:81](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md#L81) (§2.4) |
| M5 | Attested with cryptographic non-repudiation | [docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md:91](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md#L91) (§2.5) |
| M6 | Bias-displaced via a **verified heterogeneous reflection boundary** | [docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md:103](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md#L103) (§2.6; operator's binding interpretation) |
| M7 | LLM-agnostic at every cognitive boundary | [docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md:128](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md#L128) (§2.7) |

These strategic properties do not dilute the primary bar. The strategy itself identifies an unresolved verification gap for decorrelated model families: naming two providers, signing their labels or using distinct cryptographic roles cannot establish independent training or errors. Operator-controlled, recoverable stop under M3 is compatible with RL3; an external entitlement or vendor outage that disables local custody is not. Historical strategy claims are requirements and context, not current execution receipts. [docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md:113](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/docs/strategy/moonshot-synthesis.md#L113); N8 §P2-31 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N8-VOTE-CHIEF-ARCHITECT.md:446`); N9 §P2-35 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N9-VOTE-COMPETITIVE-STRATEGIST.md:597`).

### III.2 — TABLE 5: four-pillar North Star ranking

Scores and TOTAL below are copied from `TALLY.json.northstar`, without rerating or canonicalizing names. Scale: **0** absent in the inspected boundary; **1** documentary/fragmentary/optional support; **2** implemented mechanisms with material gaps; **3** substantial source-supported delivery without complete operational qualification; **4** reproducible adversarial delivery with a remaining qualification; **5** fully delivered, default-on and test-proven throughout the declared boundary. **n/a** means insufficient evidence, never failed behavior. Fractional values are medians, not measured performance. See [N9 scoring rubric](N9-VOTE-COMPETITIVE-STRATEGIST.md) and [binding tally](TALLY.json).

**Data caveats:** the tally contains **131 rows**, including ai-memory, with **78 numeric TOTALs and 53 unranked n/a TOTALs**. KIP / KIP–LDC Labs, mem0 / Mem0–OpenMemory / mem0–OpenMemory, and agentmemory aliases overlap; preserve them because the tally is binding, but do not count them as independent products or independent evidence. TOTAL sums available scores, so it is sensitive to evidence coverage and is not a safety pass, normalized market score or vendor procurement ranking. Unknown-heavy closed systems cannot be declared inferior from this arithmetic. Equal TOTALs share competition rank; alphabetical order breaks display ties. Table 5b retains exactly the same row order.

Pillar subtotals are derived sums of known cells, with **†** marking incomplete coverage; all-unknown pillars remain n/a. EN1 is separately scored and included once in TOTAL. #### Do competitors address the North Star?

**Yes, in parts; no assessed system establishes the complete bar.** Under the stated full-delivery threshold of 5, **no competitor demonstrably meets any of DI1, DI2, DI3, SE1, SE2, PF1, PF2, PF3, RL1, RL2 or EN1**; their highest medians are 2. RL3 peaks at 3 (KIP / LDC Labs), still short of complete operational qualification. This is a bounded evidence conclusion, not proof that every implementation fails every criterion. In the secondary anchor, **no verified M6 boundary is established** (maximum 1). DI3/M5 are not unique to ai-memory: Vestige and ContextLattice score 2 with real receipts/anchors, but incomplete enforcement. [Tally](TALLY.json); Vestige source dossier (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/us3x3/U1-DOSSIER-U06-Vestige.md`); ContextLattice source dossier (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/us3x3/U1-DOSSIER-U07-ContextLattice.md`); advantage audit's rejected claims (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/adv3x3/AI-MEMORY-COMPETITIVE-ADVANTAGE-CODE-LEVEL-2026-09-27.md:1898`).

The EN1 score of 2 is not an exception to its requirement.

Broader competitive gaps survive equal criterion scores. OpenViking leads in unified enterprise identity, real remote MCP and per-role configuration; KIP leads in epistemic/query-privacy structure; MemPalace preserves searchable originals; managed offerings retain the documented procurement advantages in the US audit. This plan targets their concrete behaviors rather than treating the North Star total as a replacement for buyer evidence. “Where ai-memory is behind” (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/comp3x7/COMPETITOR-ASSESSMENT-3x7-2026-09-27.md:346`), OpenViking leads (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ov3x3/AI-MEMORY-VS-OPENVIKING-3x3-CODE-LEVEL-2026-09-27.md:181`), US market conclusion (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/us3x3/US-AGENT-MEMORY-MARKET-3x3-AUDIT-2026-09-27.md`).

The advantage tally classifies **182 mechanisms: 84 UNIQUE, 34 RARE, 64 TABLE-STAKES, zero NOT-REAL**. Preserve that result. The critics' NOT-REAL allegations and final downgraded-claim section still defeat claims of universal convergence, atomic fleet commit, complete signed audit, independent destructive judging, default air gap and total backend parity. A real primitive is not proof of its strongest marketing interpretation. Advantage tally (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/adv3x3/TALLY.json`), rejected claims (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/adv3x3/AI-MEMORY-COMPETITIVE-ADVANTAGE-CODE-LEVEL-2026-09-27.md:1898`).

### III.3 — Every MUST-V1.1 acceptance package

#### Shared TEST-PROVEN protocol G

Each gate below has two independent outcomes: **correctness qualification** and **competitive superiority**. Neither is claimed executed here. The retained proposal, evidence-skeptic correction and final-voter acceptance source are linked per item; the narrower supported scope and stricter measurable gate control. The tally controls priority, including P2-31 even though one voter merged it.

1. Freeze product/edition/commit, actual distributed binary digest, configuration, backend, host/OS, hardware, model/revision, corpus, workload, seeds, limits and complete operation/sink inventory before testing. Test both ai-memory stores and every advertised required surface. A skipped required cell is INCOMPLETE. Compare rivals' documented default and strongest appropriate configurations separately.
2. Use an independent expected-state/authority/digest oracle. Inject crashes, timeout, partition, stale revision, replay, signer/authority failure and malformed input at the relevant boundaries. Every safety test also has authorized useful-work controls; refusing all work earns no win. Source inspection and an issue closure do not count as a pass.
3. Compare supported logical buyer operations at equal durability, authorization, signing obligation, encryption, inference/token/dollar budget, retained data and quality floors. Include all failures, abstentions, retries, deferred indexing/readiness and overhead. Missing features are Unsupported; inaccessible products are Unmeasured; private internals remain Unknown. None counts as an observed corrupt outcome.
4. For a correctness win, ai-memory must have zero forbidden outcomes and strictly fewer matched violations, or strictly greater externally verifiable coverage without lower useful completion. If both systems pass, record PARITY. For measured improvements, meet the item's margin and a paired 95% confidence interval excluding no improvement; preregister sample size/power, seeds and multiple-comparison handling. A zero-failure finite test bounds observed behavior; it is not a universal impossibility proof.
5. Publish raw machine-readable receipts, denominators, exact failures, cost/latency/quality distributions and reproduction commands. Every named comparator gets its own PASS-WIN / PARITY / LOSS / UNSUPPORTED / UNMEASURED result. No transfer of managed-service scores to OSS, later-branch fixes to this pin, or same-model votes to independent experiments. Engineering tests do not establish authorization or certification.

This protocol follows [N5 evidence corrections](N5-CRITIQUE-EVIDENCE-SKEPTIC.md), [N8 protocol G](N8-VOTE-CHIEF-ARCHITECT.md) and [N9 protocol G](N9-VOTE-COMPETITIVE-STRATEGIST.md). A correct release may still lose a competitive test; repair completion and superiority claims remain separate.

<a id="p1-05"></a>

#### P1-05 — Complete generation and evidence provenance

**Problem/evidence.** A kind/provenance label does not reconstruct the source revision, generator configuration or complete evidence for a derived artifact. [src/models/memory.rs:64](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/models/memory.rs#L64); C:226 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/comp3x7/COMPETITOR-ASSESSMENT-3x7-2026-09-27.md:226`); N1 §P1-05 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N1-PROPOSE-COMPETITIVE-GAPS.md:156`); N9 §P1-05 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N9-VOTE-COMPETITIVE-STRATEGIST.md:212`). **Proposal.** Commit a signed GenerationRun and immutable source-revision links with every existing derivation. Separate Complete from Incomplete/Unknown and retain canonical evidence separately from display redaction. Freeze a role-receipt schema now; the complete role router is not a prerequisite. **Tenets:** DI1, DI2, DI3, RL1, M2, M4, M5, M6, M7. **Competitors to defeat:** TencentDB-Agent-Memory, cognee; no defeat claimed yet. **TEST-PROVEN acceptance — NOT RUN:** For 10,000 existing derivations under persistence faults, every committed output links to exact retained source revisions and a signed run; missing fields are Incomplete, never Complete. Zero orphaned or falsely complete artifacts. On the identical supported transformation trace, achieve a strictly higher independently verifiable complete-lineage fraction than each named comparator; include all committed outputs in the denominator. Unknown/Incomplete earns no Complete numerator credit; compare equal successful generation yield. **Effort/dependencies:** M; P3-01, P3-06, P3-13. **Existing issue carriers:** [#4096](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4096), [#4104](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4104), [#3575](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/3575); extend these scopes and their linked regression issues, do not duplicate them.

<a id="p2-04"></a>

#### P2-04 — Make acknowledgement mean power-loss durability

**Problem/evidence.** SQLite defaults to NORMAL; aborting a process does not exercise loss of unflushed storage writes. [src/storage/connection.rs:542](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/connection.rs#L542); [src/write_receipt.rs:54](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/write_receipt.rs#L54); C:360 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/comp3x7/COMPETITOR-ASSESSMENT-3x7-2026-09-27.md:360`); N2 §P2-04 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N2-PROPOSE-NORTH-STAR-DELIVERY.md:136`); N9 §P2-04 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N9-VOTE-COMPETITIVE-STRATEGIST.md:531`). **Proposal.** Make the mission-critical durability setting explicit and verified before writes; distinguish local durability, replica acknowledgements and incomplete quorum in receipts. Qualify the actual filesystem/device stack with an external acknowledged-digest ledger and hard resets. **Tenets:** DI1, DI2, RL2. **Competitors to defeat:** agentmemory, TencentDB-Agent-Memory; no defeat claimed yet. **TEST-PROVEN acceptance — NOT RUN:** Run at least 100 randomized hard-reset trials per admitted backend/storage stack with an independent acknowledged digest/revision oracle; zero acknowledged loss or altered revisions in the declared durable profile. A process abort alone fails this gate. Against agentmemory and TencentDB-Agent-Memory require strictly lower ACK-loss rate at equivalent durability settings; ties are parity. Report local/replica ACK and incomplete quorum separately. The reset fixture must actually discard unflushed writes; otherwise label the outcome VM-reset persistence only and state flush assumptions. **Effort/dependencies:** L; P3-01, P3-06. **Existing issue carriers:** [#3559](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/3559), [#3561](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/3561); extend these scopes and their linked regression issues, do not duplicate them.

<a id="p2-16"></a>

#### P2-16 — Enforce privacy before capture, inference, tracing and export

**Problem/evidence.** Credential regexes and filtering after inference cannot enforce private-span confidentiality across capture, diagnostics and export. [src/secret_screen.rs:150](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/secret_screen.rs#L150); [src/secret_screen.rs:597](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/secret_screen.rs#L597); A:2396 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/adv3x3/A5-REFUTE-AI-MEMORY-REALITY.md:2396`); N2 §P2-16 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N2-PROPOSE-NORTH-STAR-DELIVERY.md:400`); N9 §P2-16 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N9-VOTE-COMPETITIVE-STRATEGIST.md:563`). **Proposal.** Apply deterministic protected-span screening before any external call. Refuse on screening failure, export secret references, and preserve protected canonical signed bytes while emitting safe diagnostic projections. Universal PII recognition and semantic-poison immunity remain unproved. **Tenets:** SE1, SE2, EN1, M1. **Competitors to defeat:** OpenViking, Haystack, agentmemory; no defeat claimed yet. **TEST-PROVEN acceptance — NOT RUN:** Across every current capture/embed/model/log/webhook/export sink and every byte/nesting position in bounded inputs, seeded explicitly protected canaries never leave the permitted boundary, including scanner failure; allowed controls remain intact and signed original bytes verify. Fewer leakage cases than each named comparator on the shared canary/fault suite is required for a win. Semantic poisoning success requires its own held-out #3570 results.  **Effort/dependencies:** L; P3-03, P3-11, P3-13. **Existing issue carriers:** [#4105](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4105), [#4104](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4104), [#4106](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4106), [#4103](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4103); extend these scopes and their linked regression issues, do not duplicate them.

<a id="p2-31"></a>

#### P2-31 — Make record-stop a cross-process commit fence with recoverable resume

**Problem/evidence.** A handwritten read-only inventory and process-local checks cannot establish a cross-process stop fence. Point fixes at the pin do not prove complete coverage. [src/storage/record_stop.rs:278](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/record_stop.rs#L278); [src/storage/record_stop.rs:345](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/blob/a1403c742f9d590a08b6fd170deec5f50ca8e940/src/storage/record_stop.rs#L345); A:2802 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/adv3x3/A5-REFUTE-AI-MEMORY-REALITY.md:2802`); N2 §P2-31 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N2-PROPOSE-NORTH-STAR-DELIVERY.md:730`); N8 §P2-31 (local evidence: `/ai-scratch/deputy/codex-pool/out/ns3x3/N8-VOTE-CHIEF-ARCHITECT.md:446`). **Proposal.** Check a durable monotone stop epoch inside every mutation transaction, including hidden maintenance. ### III.4 — FIX / IMPROVE / REDESIGN: defect classes and structural closure

The binding MUST set has **5 IMPROVE and 36 REDESIGN** items; neither SHOULD item is classified FIX/IMPROVE/REDESIGN (both are NEW-FEATURE). There is no standalone FIX-class MUST/SHOULD entry in the tally. This does not postpone repairs: the FIX column below names the immediate defect class, and the structural column names the retained owner that prevents recurrence. Each Gate link carries that item's code citations, named-rival test, effort and existing issues. Point fixes and structural completion must both retain the same regression oracle.

| Owner / original category | FIX: root defect class | IMPROVE / REDESIGN: required structural closure |
|---|---|---|
| [P1-05](#p1-05) · IMPROVE | A kind/provenance label does not reconstruct the source revision, generator configuration or complete evidence for a derived artifact. | Commit a signed GenerationRun and immutable source-revision links with every existing derivation. |
| [P2-04](#p2-04) · IMPROVE | SQLite defaults to NORMAL; aborting a process does not exercise loss of unflushed storage writes. | Make the mission-critical durability setting explicit and verified before writes; distinguish local durability, replica acknowledgements and incomplete quorum in receipts. |
| [P2-16](#p2-16) · IMPROVE | Credential regexes and filtering after inference cannot enforce private-span confidentiality across capture, diagnostics and export. | Apply deterministic protected-span screening before any external call. |
| [P2-31](#p2-31) · REDESIGN | A handwritten read-only inventory and process-local checks cannot establish a cross-process stop fence. | Check a durable monotone stop epoch inside every mutation transaction, including hidden maintenance. |
| [P2-35](#p2-35) · IMPROVE | At the pin, summary generation and fixed thresholds do not constitute an independent destructive judge. | Complete the existing decision carrier with typed Permit/Refuse/Abstain bound to source revisions, proposed effects, policy and role identity. |
| [P2-42](#p2-42) · IMPROVE | Stub competitor runners, issue counts and analyst votes do not demonstrate a mission-critical or competitive outcome. | Extend the existing mission ledger with real pinned adapters, external oracles, five-clock timing and complete failure/cost denominators. |
| [P3-01](#p3-01) · REDESIGN | Authorization, source revision, content, lifecycle, audit, quota and delivery intent cross consistency boundaries; a second writer can deadlock escalation. | Implement one transaction-backed apply operation owning the complete committed tuple. |
| [P3-02](#p3-02) · REDESIGN | Policy/lease read failures can become absence, wildcard semantics skip Deny, and mutable policy reads misbind evidence. | Publish immutable compiled PolicySnapshot epochs and typed Present/AbsentAllowedBySignedPosture/Unavailable results. |
| [P3-03](#p3-03) · REDESIGN | Principal strings, privilege booleans, raw reads and fan-out paths bypass a uniform authorization contract; empty enrollment can leave enforcement inert. | Require sealed VerifiedPrincipal and AuthorizedReadScope values at all current reads, mutations, counts, scoring, derived views and event sends. |
| [P3-04](#p3-04) · REDESIGN | Replaceable refresh caches can reinstall revoked credentials or preserve stale authorization indefinitely. | Use monotone credential/revocation epochs with bounded freshness leases and CAS publication. |
| [P3-06](#p3-06) · REDESIGN | Some successful mutations can outlive failed audit append; an optional signature or host witness does not prove the author's action. | Make role-correct SignedMutationEnvelope persistence a condition of CommitReceipt. |
| [P3-07](#p3-07) · REDESIGN | A hash chain cannot detect deletion of its own tail without an independently retained head; loose sequence checks can certify gaps. | Anchor signed store/epoch/sequence/root checkpoints in an operator-controlled independent witness. |
| [P3-08](#p3-08) · REDESIGN | Content-free summaries, stale source snapshots and premature vector retirement can turn failed inference into successful destructive replacement. | Use revision-bound semantic plans with PreserveAndDefer for missing, invalid or failed generation. |
| [P3-10](#p3-10) · REDESIGN | HTTP success is confused with usable model output; breaker completion races can reopen an obsolete probe. | Represent usable, abstain, invalid, unavailable and cancelled outcomes explicitly. |
| [P3-11](#p3-11) · REDESIGN | Doctor, reembed, artifact downloads and webhook connection construction escape a common egress decision; redirects and DNS can change the actual target. | Permit connections only through an admitted-target client factory binding parsed scheme, effective port, DNS result, policy epoch and TLS identity. |
| [P3-12](#p3-12) · REDESIGN | The pin refuses off-host plaintext inference but permits loopback HTTP; authenticated stdio/UDS metadata is not encrypted transport. | Inventory every application-data and identity/control-data hop, then provide authenticated encrypted channels and usable host adapters. |
| [P3-13](#p3-13) · REDESIGN | Handwritten schemas and wire codecs silently coerce invalid CAS fields, panic on Unicode, duplicate keys or consume the next valid frame. | Use closed typed commands, explicit Missing/Null/Value and bounded canonical codecs. |
| [P3-14](#p3-14) · REDESIGN | Mixed timestamp orderings, whole-row clock inheritance and unbounded unions make merge order-dependent and receiver-invalid. | Specify a finite versioned merge algebra with immutable operation identity, per-field causal versions and preserved conflict alternatives. |
| [P3-15](#p3-15) · REDESIGN | Null/absent cursors, premature nonce consumption and false no-op ACKs can skip accepted operations or defeat retries. | Persist operation identity and Applied/AlreadyApplied/DurablePending/TerminalRefused outcomes atomically. |
| [P3-16](#p3-16) · REDESIGN | Tombstone checks outside the write transaction race with inbound/restore; configured workers are mistaken for running erasure service. | Commit erasure epoch, row/key disposition and outbox together; every apply/restore locks and checks that epoch. |
| [P3-17](#p3-17) · REDESIGN | Matching IDs do not attest matching bytes; redaction, merge and release can disconnect signature verdicts, content and embeddings. | Verify immutable origin bytes first. |
| [P3-19](#p3-19) · REDESIGN | Derived indexes can be stale or corrupted while reporting clean; reordered projection work can resurrect removed edges. | Write revision-bound projection jobs with authoritative commits. |
| [P3-20](#p3-20) · REDESIGN | Safety traversal of an asynchronous graph can miss contaminated dependents; wrong-store access and inconsistent locks undermine containment. | Use the authoritative relational graph and one lock order for containment, cycle checks, invalidation and restore. |
| [P3-21](#p3-21) · REDESIGN | Rung-specific trigger reconstruction, counts outside conversion, nested pool acquisition and error-string matching can certify an incomplete migration. | Verify a manifest of tables, triggers, indexes, extensions and invariants before write service. |
| [P3-22](#p3-22) · REDESIGN | Archiving one predicate snapshot then deleting another loses required revision history; replay can overwrite the useful archive. | Lock exact victim IDs/revisions/digests and archive/delete that immutable set in bounded transactions. |
| [P3-23](#p3-23) · REDESIGN | Approval can commit without recoverable execution intent; database claim exclusivity does not fence an external effect. | Persist approval and execution intent together, then run an explicit retryable state machine that rechecks authority. |
| [P3-24](#p3-24) · REDESIGN | Volatile semaphore queues lose accepted deliveries; sidecar counters fabricate health and unsubscribe strands audit ownership. | Persist delivery intent before admission, lease it on the active store, recheck subscriber authority immediately before send, and preserve ownership metadata after deletion. |
| [P3-25](#p3-25) · REDESIGN | Blocking socket probes and reconnect hints can starve durable inbox reads; TTL and ownership behavior differ by backend/OS. | Track successful inbox-read deadlines independently of hints. |
| [P3-27](#p3-27) · REDESIGN | Detached writers and incomplete signal handling allow writes after a final witness or certify the wrong store. | Own every writer under a runtime supervisor: stop admission, persist intents, drain/join or fence writers, then witness/checkpoint the active store. |
| [P3-28](#p3-28) · REDESIGN | MCP SQLite affinity, PostgreSQL unsupported skills and sidecar access contradict broad parity claims. | Freeze required operation/frontend/backend/OS cells and inject immutable ActiveStore identity everywhere. |
| [P3-29](#p3-29) · REDESIGN | Blocking model work on runtime workers/DB locks and global hook serialization cause contention collapse. | Separate bounded CPU, remote inference, DB and hook queues with fair per-principal admission. |
| [P3-30](#p3-30) · REDESIGN | Per-child bounds do not bound aggregate bytes, work, fan-out, decompression or retry duration. | Carry one consumable parent budget and absolute deadline through nested work. |
| [P3-31](#p3-31) · REDESIGN | Ambient cwd/environment and late validation can target an unintended database or mutate before rejecting input. | Resolve absolute paths, store identity, configuration source, principal and clock once into RuntimeContext. |
| [P3-33](#p3-33) · REDESIGN | Text scanners miss aliasing, multiline SQL, visibility and feature-target variations; broad allowlists suppress real bypasses. | Seal privileged constructors and commit permits, add compile-fail fixtures, and execute semantic bypass plants on every supported feature target. |
| [P3-34](#p3-34) · REDESIGN | Locale-dependent comparisons, missing coverage entries and mismatched build/test artifacts can produce false release certification. | Bind required receipts to installed artifact, source/config/feature/backend/OS/fixture digests. |
| [P3-36](#p3-36) · REDESIGN | A corpus-only backup or SQLite sidecar snapshot does not recover the actual PostgreSQL service, keys, erasure floor and pending work. | Declare a signed recovery inventory and snapshot/WAL cut; orchestrate native backup on the active store, download/verify offsite bytes, restore on a clean host, then verify authority and atomically switch. |
| [P3-37](#p3-37) · REDESIGN | Direct executable overwrite and independently maintained package/service manifests make interruption or upgrade destructive. | Stage, verify, fsync, atomically publish and directory-sync binaries while preserving the prior executable. |
| [P3-38](#p3-38) · REDESIGN | Raw DSNs/titles can enter logs, optional telemetry can silently fail and unknown active-store counters look like zero. | Use typed safe fields and secret references, keep signed evidence in a separately governed canonical sink, and report value/status/last-success/store identity. |
| [P3-39](#p3-39) · REDESIGN | Ranking mixes priors with relevance, contradiction semantics differ by backend, and failed candidate generation can report confident no-match. | Share eligibility and scoring formulas, keep relevance/confidence/contradiction separate, and report evidence sufficiency plus exact token/drop accounting. |
| [P3-41](#p3-41) · REDESIGN | First-run downloads and remote configuration complicate disconnected operation; local packaging alone proves no air-gap or no-kill guarantee. | Stage and verify binary, identities, schemas, policy and model assets, with encrypted local adapters and local operator recovery. |
| [P3-42](#p3-42) · REDESIGN | Host flag/schema drift, duplicate imports and a boot sentinel alone do not prove retained context is usable across sessions. | Pin finite supported host versions and share command/principal/encrypted-channel contracts. |

The highest-risk root classes are **authority represented as optional data**, **commit effects split across stores/transactions**, **derived state treated as authoritative**, **volatile queues mistaken for durable acceptance**, **unbounded nested work**, and **claims detached from executed artifacts**. Cross-cutting contracts—not larger tool counts—close these classes. Current GA blockers remain immediate obligations; a v1.1.0 label is not permission to release a known unsafe path. #### NO and CUT

**Binding NO: P1-50 only.** Do not add optional vector backends for catalogue parity. There is no measured ai-memory bottleneck or equal-quality workload advantage that justifies another consistency/recovery plane while current projections and parity remain open. The re-entry test is **1M vectors, at least 20% higher useful goodput than mem0/Honcho/Chroma at identical recall@10, p99, ACL and durability floors**, plus zero source loss, unauthorized hits or falsely-current vectors under index outage/reorder/duplicate/rebuild. Failing to measure that win means do not ship. Existing projection/qualification scope: [#4112](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/4112), [#3568](https://github.com/alphaonedev/ai-memory-mcp/issues/3568). [P1-50 evidence](N1-PROPOSE-COMPETITIVE-GAPS.md), [N5 P1-50](N5-CRITIQUE-EVIDENCE-SKEPTIC.md), [binding tally](TALLY.json).

**The final tally has no CUT decision.** CUT is a critique action, not a fifth release priority. The following N4/N5/N6 CUT recommendations are retained as reasons to exclude expansion or consolidate it. Where the final tally says SHOULD, LATER, NO-CONSENSUS or a retained owner is MUST, that binding disposition wins; no critic's CUT silently overrides it. The linked proposal contains each named comparator and quantitative re-entry gate, retained even when no expansion ships.

### III.6 — Dependency order and critical path to test-proven wins

The release plan is a set of shared contracts and vertical slices. A contract can be frozen before every caller migrates; final conformance follows implementation. This separates design prerequisites from completion prerequisites and removes cycles such as identity ↔ parity, projection ↔ migration/restore, erasure ↔ replay, webhook ↔ shutdown and scheduler ↔ resource budget. N6's **125–216 engineering-week** estimate (including reserve) applies to its own narrowed portfolio, not automatically to this 41-item binding set; it is a planning judgment, not measured delivery time. No defensible ship date follows from these audits. [N6 sequencing/effort](N6-CRITIQUE-DELIVERY-REALIST.md:42), [N8 sequencing](N8-VOTE-CHIEF-ARCHITECT.md), [N9 strategy](N9-VOTE-COMPETITIVE-STRATEGIST.md:32).

| Order | Work and dependency exit | Test-proven exit / existing carriers |
|---|---|---|
| 0 — Freeze the test and wire contracts | P3-31 runtime/store identity; P3-28 operation matrix scaffold; P3-30 budget contract; P3-34 artifact manifest scaffold; P2-42 independent oracles/adapters. Jointly specify principal/policy/signer/commit, replication operation/cursor/erasure, projection/schema and worker lifecycle contracts. Provision baseline recovery snapshots, hard-reset rig and independent failure domains now. | Every required cell, external oracle, fixture deadline and comparator pin is enumerated; missing adapters remain explicit. #3558, #3559, #3561, #3572, #3798, #4108. |
| 1 — Close authority and transport before expansion | P3-02/03/04 policy/principal/revocation; P3-11/12 egress and EN1; P2-16 privacy; P3-13 codecs; P3-10 model outcomes. Direct repair of known default, parsing, source-preservation and installer faults proceeds immediately. | No unavailable authority becoming Allow, no wrong-scope disclosure, no plaintext supported hop, valid authorized controls remain usable. At least two real encrypted host integrations must work; incompatible clients refuse. #3794, #4097, #4099, #4100, #4103–4106, #3454. |
| 2 — Make acknowledged state trustworthy | P3-01 atomic tuple → P3-06 mandatory signed receipt → P2-04 durability and P3-07 independent tail anchor. Apply P2-31 stop, P3-08 safe replacement, P2-35 deterministic destructive clearance, P1-05 generation provenance; P3-21 migration manifests start from the baseline fixtures. | Two-process/fault schedules show zero partial, unauthorized, unsigned or lost acknowledged changes; useful work progresses. Stop/resume and model failure preserve exact source state. #4092–4096, #3559, #3561, #3569, #4111. |
| 3 — Prove replay, projections and lifecycle closure | P3-14 merge algebra → P3-15 durable apply/cursors → P3-16 erasure. P3-17 exact-byte provenance, P3-19 projections, P3-20 authoritative containment and P3-22 immutable retention build on the atomic contract. P3-23 actions, P3-24 deliveries, P3-25 wake and P3-27 supervised shutdown share durable intents. | One million merge triples, three persisted peers, complete ACK accounting, no controlled-copy resurrection, no false clean projection, no post-witness writes. External exactly-once only at tested fenced sinks. #4101, #4098, #3793, #3795, #4112, #3574, #3466. |
| 4 — Close the full supported service boundary | P3-29 useful performance and P3-39 retrieval quality after correctness; P3-36 actual-store clean-host restore; P3-37 packages/upgrades; P3-38 truthful confidential telemetry; P3-41 offline deployment; P3-42 host continuity. Finish P3-28 every-cell conformance, P3-33 structural boundary gates and P3-34 installed-artifact qualification. SHOULD P1-12/P2-34 only enter after their foundations and keep separate quality/routing evidence. | Equal-budget comparisons include all completed semantic work and failures. No skip-as-pass or API-presence-as-parity. Restore inventory, encrypted usability and host retrieval-use oracles pass. #3335, #3341, #3342, #2425, #3568, #4107–4110, #4114, #3798, #3799. |
| 5 — Publish only reproduced outcomes | P2-42 final qualification: two GA missions → all 12 retained missions, n≥30 independent seeds/arm; 24 h then 72 h qualification and separately qualified hard resets. Run each package's rival gate. Re-run artifact-bound gates on the exact release bytes after the last change. | A complete mandatory matrix with zero observed silent-loss/partial/unsigned/unauthorized/plaintext successes and all declared liveness/quality floors. Each claimed rival win must meet its preregistered margin and paired CI; publish losses, ties and missing cases. #3564, #3568, #3569, #3570, #3559, #3561. |

**Critical dependency chain:** frozen operation/authority/transport contracts → usable encrypted authenticated paths → atomic state + signed receipt → durable ACK + independent anchored history → resumable replication/erasure and authoritative projections → active-store shutdown/restore → full backend/host conformance → equal-budget missions and artifact-bound qualification. Physical-reset infrastructure, comparator adapters and clean-host recovery fixtures run alongside implementation from phase 0; leaving them until feature completion makes the claim—not merely the code—late. The phase exits inherit the concrete numerical gates in III.3; a checklist or issue closure alone cannot satisfy them.

There are two different finish lines. **Release safety** requires every retained MUST obligation in the declared supported boundary; a rival tie does not block a necessary repair or justify leaving a defect open. **“Defeat competitor X, test-proven”** requires an accessible pinned X deployment, a supported shared task, zero mandatory ai-memory safety regression, and a strict preregistered outcome win with reproducible receipts. Closed or unavailable rivals remain Unmeasured; a disconnected requirement gap is labeled Unsupported. A universal defeat claim remains unavailable while those cells are unknown. [Protocol G](#shared-test-proven-protocol-g), [P2-42](#p2-42), [US audit limits](../us3x3/US-AGENT-MEMORY-MARKET-3x3-AUDIT-2026-09-27.md).
